body:
## Implemented Vercel Speed Insights Integration

### Summary
Successfully integrated Vercel Speed Insights into the portfolio project. The project is a static HTML portfolio, so the HTML implementation of Speed Insights was used as specified in the Vercel documentation.

### Changes Made

#### Modified Files:
- **index.html** - Added Vercel Speed Insights tracking scripts

### Implementation Details

Added the following scripts before the closing `</body>` tag in index.html:

```html
<!-- Vercel Speed Insights -->
<script>
  window.si = window.si || function () { (window.siq = window.siq || []).push(arguments); };
</script>
<script defer src="/_vercel/speed-insights/script.js"></script>
```

### Why This Approach

1. **Static HTML Project**: The repository contains a pure static HTML portfolio with no build process, package managers, or frameworks.

2. **HTML Implementation**: According to the Vercel Speed Insights documentation, HTML projects require a simple script tag implementation without any npm package installation. This approach:
   - Adds minimal overhead
   - Requires no build configuration
   - Works immediately after deployment to Vercel
   - Enables the `/_vercel/speed-insights/script.js` route (automatically provided by Vercel)

3. **Code Placement**: The scripts are placed just before the closing `</body>` tag as specified in the documentation, ensuring:
   - The DOM is fully loaded before the tracking script runs
   - The script is loaded with `defer` attribute for non-blocking execution
   - Proper integration with the existing page scripts

### Next Steps

After deployment to Vercel:
1. The `/_vercel/speed-insights/*` routes will be automatically available
2. Speed Insights data collection will begin automatically
3. Performance metrics can be viewed in the Vercel dashboard under the Speed Insights tab
4. Data will be available after a few days of visitor traffic

### Notes

- No npm package installation needed for static HTML
- The implementation follows the exact pattern from the official Vercel Speed Insights documentation
- The tracking is non-intrusive and has minimal performance impact
- Vercel will automatically enable Speed Insights routes upon deployment

author: seijikohara
body:
## Summary

- Split publish into separate jobs with isolated OIDC tokens
- Use matrix strategy for framework packages to reduce duplication
- Each job gets its own OIDC token, preventing token expiration

## Problem

npm provenance uses OIDC tokens that expire after a single publish operation. When publishing multiple packages sequentially (even with `pnpm publish -r`), the token expires after the first package:

```
npm notice Access token expired or revoked.
npm error 404 Not Found - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/@vizel%2freact
```

## Solution

```
build → publish-core → publish-framework (matrix: react/vue/svelte) → finalize
```

- **build**: Build all packages, upload artifacts
- **publish-core**: Publish @vizel/core first (fresh OIDC token)
- **publish-framework**: Publish react/vue/svelte in parallel via matrix (each gets fresh OIDC token)
- **finalize**: Commit version changes, create git tag and GitHub release

## Benefits

- Each publish job has its own OIDC token (no expiration issues)
- Framework packages publish in parallel (faster)
- Matrix reduces code duplication
- Provenance support maintained for supply chain security

## Test plan

- [ ] Run publish workflow with 0.0.1-alpha.4

author: dshkol
body:
## Summary

Performance optimizations for caching and I/O operations.

### Changes

**P3: list_cansim_cached_tables single-pass optimization**
- Consolidate three separate `lapply()` calls into a single iteration over cached table paths
- Collects `timeCached`, `rawSize`, and `title` in one pass per cached table
- Avoids repeated `dir()` calls and file read operations that were being done 3x per path
- Use `vapply()` for type-safe extraction from collected metadata

**P10: Avoid unnecessary tibble conversion**
- Check `tibble::is_tibble()` before calling `as_tibble()`
- Skips conversion when data is already a tibble

### Files Modified

- `R/cansim.R`: tibble conversion check
- `R/cansim_parquet.R`: single-pass cache metadata collection

---

## Benchmark Notes

### P3: list_cansim_cached_tables - Not directly benchmarked

**Reason**: Requires a populated cache directory with multiple cached tables to meaningfully benchmark.

**Expected improvement**: The optimization reduces file I/O operations from 3N to N (where N is number of cached tables):

```r
# Before: Three separate lapply calls, each reading files
result$timeCached <- lapply(result$path, function(p) { ... })  # Read 1
result$rawSize <- lapply(result$path, function(p) { ... })     # Read 2  
result$title <- lapply(result$path, function(p) { ... })       # Read 3

# After: Single pass collecting all metadata
cache_metadata <- lapply(result$path, function(p) {
  # Collect timeCached, rawSize, title in one pass
  list(timeCached = ..., rawSize = ..., title = ...)
})
result$timeCached <- do.call("c", lapply(cache_metadata, `[[`, "timeCached"))
result$rawSize <- vapply(cache_metadata, `[[`, numeric(1), "rawSize")
result$title <- vapply(cache_metadata, `[[`, character(1), "title")
```

**To benchmark manually**:
```r
library(microbenchmark)
library(cansim)

# First, populate cache with several tables:
cache_path <- "~/.cansim_cache"
for (tbl in c("34-10-0013", "17-10-0005", "14-10-0287")) {
  get_cansim_sqlite(tbl, cache_path = cache_path)
}

# Benchmark (run on master, then on optimized branch)
microbenchmark(
  list_cached = list_cansim_cached_tables(cache_path = cache_path),
  times = 20
)
```

---

### P10: tibble conversion check - Not directly benchmarked

**Reason**: Negligible impact - this is primarily a code quality improvement.

**Analysis**: The `is_tibble()` check is O(1) and very fast. Most data flowing through `normalize_cansim_values()` is already a tibble from prior processing, so the `as_tibble()` call was largely unnecessary. The improvement is in avoiding the conversion overhead when data is already the correct type.

```r
# Before
data <- as_tibble(data)

# After
if (!tibble::is_tibble(data)) data <- as_tibble(data)
```

---

### Deferred Optimizations

**P6 (field cache utilization)**: Evaluated but not implemented
- The audit plan referenced "field cache written but never read" at lines 254-263
- Could not identify a specific field cache location in the current code structure
- May require further investigation or the referenced caching pattern may have changed

**P7 (csv2sqlite transform copies)**: Evaluated but not implemented
- Using conditional piping `{if (...) ... else .}` would harm code readability
- The current conditional structure is clearer and the performance gain (~25-40%) is minor
- Trade-off favors maintainability over micro-optimization

---

## Summary

| Optimization | Benchmarked | Expected Impact | Status |
|--------------|-------------|-----------------|--------|
| P3 (single-pass) | Manual setup required | Reduces I/O 3x→1x | ✅ Implemented |
| P10 (tibble check) | N/A | Negligible | ✅ Implemented |

### Test Plan

- [x] `devtools::check()` passes (0 errors, 0 warnings)
- [x] All existing tests pass
- [ ] Manual testing with cached tables to verify metadata extraction

author: prajitdas
body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/prajitdas/prajitdas.github.io/security/code-scanning/48](https://github.com/prajitdas/prajitdas.github.io/security/code-scanning/48)

In general, the fix is to avoid treating arbitrary untrusted HTTP headers as trustworthy identifiers for a hosting provider based on substring or simple prefix checks. Instead, use the actual request URL (which in this script is `base_url`, provided by the user) and perform a hostname-based allowlist check or exact match on known GitHub Pages hostnames. This mirrors the recommendation to parse and check a URL’s host rather than looking for substrings.

For this script, the simplest non‑breaking change is:

- Stop inferring GitHub Pages from the `Server` header.
- Instead, parse `base_url` with `urllib.parse.urlparse` (we must add this import) and treat the host as GitHub Pages if it matches known GitHub Pages domains:
  - `github.io` (user and project pages),
  - `github.com` (for completeness if someone points directly there),
  - optionally `localhost` / `127.0.0.1` remain handled as in the current code.

Concretely, inside `main()` near lines 271–281:

- Keep the try/except and `requests.get` if you still want to confirm the URL is reachable, but remove the `server_header_normalized` and `startswith('github.com')` logic.
- Add an import at the top: `from urllib.parse import urlparse`.
- Inside the GitHub Pages detection block, compute `parsed_url = urlparse(base_url)` and `hostname = (parsed_url.hostname or '').lower()`.
- Define `is_github_pages` as `hostname.endswith('.github.io') or hostname == 'github.io' or hostname == 'github.com'`.
- Keep the `is_localhost` computation as-is or re-use `hostname in ('localhost', '127.0.0.1')` if you prefer, but to minimize changes we’ll maintain the existing `startswith` checks on `base_url` for localhost.

This preserves existing behavior for localhost, removes the unsafe reliance on a spoofable header, and aligns the detection with the URL’s host, which is what the user chose as the target.

body:
This pull request introduces several improvements and refactorings across the codebase, focusing on exception handling, workflow automation, and user interface enhancements. The most significant changes include a comprehensive overhaul of the application's exception hierarchy, the addition of a GitHub Actions workflow for publishing to PyPI, and improvements to dialogs and player data import logic.

**Exception Handling Improvements:**

* Refactored `src/gambitpairing/exceptions.py` to introduce a new, structured exception hierarchy. All custom exceptions now inherit from a new base class `GambitPairingException`, with specific subclasses for pairing, tournament, player, result, validation, resource, API, and configuration errors. This enables more granular and unified error handling throughout the application.

**Workflow Automation:**

* Added a new GitHub Actions workflow in `.github/workflows/python-publish.yml` that builds and publishes the Python package to PyPI automatically when a release is created. This streamlines the release process and ensures consistent package deployment.

**User Interface and Dialog Enhancements:**

* Improved the `ManualPairingDialog` by disabling floating for the player pool dock widget to prevent detachment issues and adding an `_auto_pair_selected_player` method, allowing users to auto-pair a selected player with the best available opponent based on rating. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-eb69fa93dda118e880fb7ce0e9e4c55968b43de5c1c142a36460c29341eeb1b8R800-L802) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-eb69fa93dda118e880fb7ce0e9e4c55968b43de5c1c142a36460c29341eeb1b8R1510-R1549)
* Updated `PlayerManagementDialog` to use API adapter functions for importing player data, standardizing field population, improving gender and date-of-birth handling, and providing clearer user notifications. Also improved the copy-to-clipboard functionality and fallback icon handling for the copy button. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9ff812b66da4799b8b6e94c1f81b3d6785730eb6b9f9f942bfbc40728203d6c0R8-R19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9ff812b66da4799b8b6e94c1f81b3d6785730eb6b9f9f942bfbc40728203d6c0L797-R856) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-9ff812b66da4799b8b6e94c1f81b3d6785730eb6b9f9f942bfbc40728203d6c0L402-R410) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-9ff812b66da4799b8b6e94c1f81b3d6785730eb6b9f9f942bfbc40728203d6c0L351-R357) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-9ff812b66da4799b8b6e94c1f81b3d6785730eb6b9f9f942bfbc40728203d6c0L387-R393)
* Added `PrintOptionsDialog` to the list of available dialogs, making it accessible in the GUI. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7dbb877b2d06874f338cf2eb52aa0a8bd1a474c448009039ac21399ee7697710R23) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7dbb877b2d06874f338cf2eb52aa0a8bd1a474c448009039ac21399ee7697710R36)

**Project Metadata and Configuration:**

* Updated project URLs in `pyproject.toml` to reflect the new repository location. Also added dynamic versioning using the `gambitpairing.__version__` attribute for setuptools compatibility. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711L54-R55) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711R90-R92)

## Summary

This PR improves the JEngine.Core package with proper namespace configuration, fixes type ambiguity, and adds test runner integration.

### Changes

**Assembly Definition Updates:**
- Added `rootNamespace: "JEngine.Core"` to `JEngine.Core.asmdef` (Runtime)
- Added `rootNamespace: "JEngine.Core"` to `JEngine.Core.Editor.asmdef` (Editor)
- Added Unity Test Framework reference to editor asmdef

**SettingsUIBuilder.cs - Fix ObjectField Ambiguity:**
- Removed unused `using UnityEditor.Search;`
- Removed `using UnityEditor.UIElements;`
- Added `using ObjectField = UnityEditor.UIElements.ObjectField;` to resolve type ambiguity between different ObjectField types

**New TestRunnerCallbacks:**
- `Editor/Misc/TestRunnerCallbacks.cs` - Implements `ICallbacks` interface for Unity Test Runner
- Provides `IsRunningTests` static property to detect when Play Mode tests are running
- Useful for systems that need to behave differently during test execution

### Why This Matters

author: mason-sharp
body:
Log in spock.resolutions when we receive a DELETE that is older than
the existing row (the DELETE was processed late).

Prior to this, the DELETE would be processed and the existing row deleted.
Now we can ignore since the timestamp is older.

While we are harmonizing conflict types with Postgres, no such type
exists for a late DELETE, so a new one was created, SPOCK_CT_DELETE_LATE.
To accommodate, moved to Spock having its own conflict types, while trying
to match those in Postgres for the large overlap.

Also added spock.output_delay GUC to make internal testing easier for
this case and future testing. It optionally adds a delay to the output plugin in
the begin callback and is used by a new test that was added. That is, one
can execute SQL on one node, then execute other SQL on another while
knowing that the earlier operations will arrive afterwards and create conflicts.

body:
## Fix SDL/MPV OpenGL Context Switching Causing Video Flicker

### Summary
- Create a dedicated SDL window for MPV's OpenGL context to prevent context switching conflicts between the main VR rendering thread and the MPV rendering thread
- Add synchronization (`glFinish()`) after MPV rendering to ensure frames are visible before buffer swap
- Add extensive debug logging infrastructure with `--mpv-debug` flag for troubleshooting

### Changes

**Core Fix:**
- Introduced a separate `m_pMpvWindow` SDL window for MPV's OpenGL context instead of sharing the companion window
- Updated `set_current_context()` to route each GL context to its appropriate window
- Moved `mpvBuffers->swap_buffer()` to after rendering completes and added `glFinish()` to ensure frame synchronization
- Added `render_update()` check to skip rendering when no new frame is available

**MPV Configuration:**
- Fixed `--mpv-profile` to only default to "gpu-hq" when `--use-system-mpv-config` is NOT set
- Set MPV options before `mpv_initialize()` and properties after for correct initialization order
- Added fallback for `mpv_render_context_create` if advanced control fails

**New Command Line Options:**
- `--mpv-debug` — Enable verbose libmpv logging
- `--reduce-flicker-amount <amount>` — Jitter amount in radians (default: 0.0005)
- `--reduce-flicker-speed <speed>` — Jitter speed (default: 1.0)

**Debug Infrastructure:**
- Added timestamped logging macros (`LOG_FUNC`, `LOG_MSG`, `LOG_ERR`, `MPV_LOG`, `WT_LOG`)
- Comprehensive logging throughout initialization, main loop, MPV events, and window texture operations

### Test plan
- [ ] Play a video with `--video` option and verify no flickering occurs
- [ ] Test with `--mpv-debug` to verify logging output
- [ ] Verify `--reduce-flicker-amount` and `--reduce-flicker-speed` options work correctly
- [ ] Test with and without `--use-system-mpv-config` to ensure profile defaults are correct

author: loci-dev
body:
Mirrored from openssl/openssl#29711

And make the provided bit string argument const.

The implicit trunction behaviour allows you to set a value without keeping the unused bits consistent, using ASN1_STRING_set, and then have it magically "fixed" to account for the unused bits in the last octet on output.

As it turns out, after much searching, nothing is using this behaviour, As long as you are setting values in a bit string
with the correct API's instead of clobbering a value in with ASN1_STRING_set, you are fine, and the implicit trunctaion
is not needed

See discussion in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/29185 and in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/29117

body:
### Motivation
- Hotel bar segments that span across rows could be mis-classified as `middle` instead of `end` when part of the range is clipped by the visible calendar window, causing missing right-side rounding and incorrect styling. 
- Add inspect/log output to make it easy to verify per-hotel segment `position` values during runtime. 
- Ensure assets are refreshed by bumping the service worker cache when layout/CSS behavior changes.

### Description
- In `buildCalendarHotelRowSegments` compute `fullRangeStartKey`/`fullRangeEndKey` and use `visibleStartKey`/`visibleEndKey` for the clipped date keys while using the full-range bounds to determine `isRangeStart`/`isRangeEnd` so final segments get `position: 'end'` when appropriate. 
- Collect per-hotel `hotelSegments` and emit a `console.debug('[calendar] hotel row segments', ...)` object listing `startKey`, `endKey`, `position`, and `weekIndex` for inspection. 
- Add CSS rule `.calendar-row-hotel-segment.is-end` to re-enable right-side border-radius for row-level hotel segments so ending segments render rounded on the right. 
- Bump service worker cache id from `acpay-v429` to `acpay-v430` in `sw.js` to ensure new assets are fetched.

### Testing

author: mattleibow
body:
This pull request significantly updates and clarifies the SkiaSharp release process documentation. It replaces the old branching and release checklist documents with a comprehensive, step-by-step release guide, and introduces two new "skills" for automating and confirming release branch creation and tagging. The changes aim to make the release process more robust, auditable, and safer by enforcing explicit user confirmation at each step.

**Key changes include:**

### Release Process Documentation Overhaul

* Completely rewrote `documentation/releasing.md` to provide a detailed, step-by-step release guide, including branch creation, version bumping, CI verification, tagging, and milestone closure. The new guide replaces the old checklist format and incorporates branching strategy and reference tables for key files and pipelines.
* Updated the documentation index (`documentation/README.md`) to reflect the new, comprehensive release guide and removed reference to the old branching strategy document.
* Removed the outdated `documentation/branching.md` file, consolidating all branching and release strategy information into the new release guide.

### Automated and Auditable Release Workflows

* Added `.github/skills/release-branch/SKILL.md`: Defines a confirmation-based, stepwise workflow for creating release branches, updating version labels, and bumping main for preview releases. Enforces explicit user confirmation at each step and documents the branching logic for preview, stable, and hotfix releases.
* Added `.github/skills/release-tag/SKILL.md`: Documents a confirmation-driven workflow for finalizing releases after packages are published, including tagging, drafting GitHub releases, and closing milestones. Details tag formats for all release types and ensures tags are only created after package verification.

author: copilot
body:
The seasons processing loop uses `pending_episodes` and `show_batch_index` without initialization, causing `UnboundLocalError` when the loop runs independently of the earlier shows processing loop.

## Changes

- Initialize `pending_episodes` and `show_batch_index` at the start of each show iteration in the seasons processing loop
- Ensures variables are scoped per-show, preventing episodes from different shows being batched together

```python
# Process seasons
for show in shows_section.all():
    if not isinstance(show, Show):
        continue
    
    show_title = getattr(show, "title", str(show))
    # Initialize variables to avoid unbound errors
    pending_episodes: list[Episode] = []
    show_batch_index = 0
    pending_seasons: list[Season] = []
    
    # ... rest of season processing
```

Addresses feedback from #226.

## What was changed
- Fix `TemporalWorker::ExecuteAsync(Func<Task>)` swallowing exceptions

## Why?
The non-generic `ExecuteAsync(Func<Task>)` overload was using `ContinueWith` with `TaskContinuationOptions.OnlyOnRanToCompletion`. When the caller's task threw an exception, this option prevented the continuation from running, causing the continuation task to be canceled rather than faulted. This resulted in `TaskCanceledException` being thrown instead of the original exception (e.g., `WorkflowFailedException`).

body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a new ZSH keyboard shortcuts discovery command that helps users learn and reference ZLE (ZSH Line Editor) keybindings. The command intelligently detects the user's shell configuration (Emacs vs Vi mode) and platform (macOS, Linux, Windows) to display contextually relevant shortcuts with proper formatting.

## Changes

### New Features
- **ZSH Keyboard Command**: Added `forge zsh keyboard` command to display platform-aware keyboard shortcuts
- **Mode Detection**: Automatically detects Vi/Vim vs Emacs keybindings from user's `.zshrc` configuration
- **Platform Detection**: Adjusts terminology based on OS (e.g., "Option" on macOS vs "Alt" on Linux/Windows)
- **Real-time Streaming**: Implements streaming output for immediate user feedback
- **Comprehensive Coverage**: Includes shortcuts for navigation, editing, history, and mode switching (for Vi mode)

### Implementation Details
- Added `ZshCommandGroup::Keyboard` CLI command variant in `crates/forge_main/src/cli.rs`
- Implemented `on_zsh_keyboard()` UI handler with spinner management in `crates/forge_main/src/ui.rs`
- Created `run_zsh_keyboard()` function with subprocess execution and line-by-line streaming in `crates/forge_main/src/zsh/plugin.rs`
- Embedded standalone ZSH script at `shell-plugin/keyboard.zsh` with ANSI formatting and intelligent detection logic
- Added comprehensive test coverage for the new command in `crates/forge_main/src/cli.rs`

### Cleanup
- **Dependency Removal**: Removed unused `forge_inte` dependency from workspace `Cargo.toml`

## Technical Highlights

- Uses embedded script content with `include_str!` for zero-dependency distribution
- Spawns ZSH subprocess with piped stdout/stderr for streaming output
- Multi-threaded line-by-line streaming using `BufReader` and thread handles
- Sources user's `.zshrc` to detect actual keybinding configuration
- Graceful error handling with proper context messages

## Files Changed
- `Cargo.toml` - Removed forge_inte dependency
- `crates/forge_main/src/cli.rs` - Added Keyboard command and test
- `crates/forge_main/src/ui.rs` - Added keyboard command handler
- `crates/forge_main/src/zsh/mod.rs` - Exported run_zsh_keyboard function
- `crates/forge_main/src/zsh/plugin.rs` - Implemented keyboard shortcuts logic
- `shell-plugin/keyboard.zsh` - New embedded ZSH script with formatting and detection

- Updated detection logic in `app.js` to scan the top lines of each page for a `Chap.` pattern, accumulate chapter entries with start pages, and deduplicate consecutive identical headers via `lastChapterKey`.
- Added detection for `Problems` using a `problemsPattern` and, when the new `Include Problems` checkbox is unchecked, stop detection before the problems section and cap the final module end page accordingly.
- Exposed a new checkbox input `#includeProblems` in `index.html` and wired it to the detection flow via `includeProblemsToggle`; updated the detection status text to reflect when detection was stopped before Problems.
- Added UI styling for the option control in `styles.css` to match the app (class `option-row` and checkbox styles).

### Testing
- Performed an automated smoke check by starting a local HTTP server and running a Playwright script that loaded `http://127.0.0.1:8000` and captured a screenshot, which completed successfully.
- No unit tests were added or run for the new parsing logic.

author: snissn
body:
fastBase.resetBase() previously appended/copy'd dict.content into history on every Reset(dict, ...), making small independent frame encoding dominated by runtime.memmove.

Cache the dict prefix in the encoder history and reuse it across resets when dict id/size match; invalidate the cache when history slides or the buffer is reallocated.

Micro-bench (Apple M3): BenchmarkEncodeAllPrewarmed_DictResetCost_1KiB/EncodeAll/std=1 ~1117 ns/op -> ~361 ns/op.

💡 What: Optimized `LearnerController.GetAllLearners` to use `GetOrdinal` for column access.

author: hansoojeongsj
body:
# 🔍 요약

- 바텀시트의 사용성을 높이기 위해 스냅 지점(Half)의 높이를 조정하고, 대사관·환전소의 상세 UI를 구현했습니다.
- 사용자가 지도를 탐색하다가 즉시 복귀할 수 있는 '내 위치로 이동' 기능을 추가했습니다.

# 🔃 변경사항

- 변경사항에 대해 자세히 설명해주세요
1. 바텀시트 개선
Snap Point 수정: 콘텐츠 가독성을 위해 half 상태의 시트 높이를 기존 50%에서 화면의 65% 노출(0.35 위치)로 조정했어요.

2. 상세 UI 구현
도메인 컨텐츠 구현
대사관: 사용자 국적에 맞춘 단일 정보 및 주의사항 안내 UI를 적용했어요.
환전소: 고유 ID(key) 기반의 리스트 렌더링과 구분선(border-b) 및 여백을 최적화했어요.
스크롤 최적화: useLayoutEffect를 사용하여 시트 이동 시 깜빡임을 방지하고, overscroll-behavior: contain으로 배경 지도와의 스크롤 간섭을 차단했어요.

3. 지도 인터랙션 (Locate My Position)
부드러운 시점 이동을 위해 forwardRef와 useImperativeHandle을 활용하여 자식 컴포넌트(NaverMap)의 기능을 캡슐화하고, 부모에서 호출 시 panTo 메서드로 '내 위치'에 부드럽게 포커싱되도록 구현했어요. 

4. 목데이터 수정
리액트의 렌더링 최적화를 위해 중복되지 않는 고유 id를 포함한 데이터셋으로 교체했어요.

# 📸 결과

- 결과를 보여주는 사진이나 로그를 첨부해주세요

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8f142ff-5f3d-41ef-b3f1-848dcfeb40a1




# ⚠️ 요청사항 or TODO

- 리뷰어에게 요청할 사항들을 작성해주세요

# 💡 이슈넘버

- JIRA 이슈 번호를 입력해주세요
- #HN-73

  * 대사관 정보가 카드 형태로 표시되고, 환전소는 항목별 카드 목록으로 제공

author: yh-05
body:
## 概要

Issue #617 の受け入れ条件を満たす `issue-management` スキルの詳細ガイド（guide.md）を拡充しました。

## 変更内容

### 1. Issue 作成手順（3モード）
- クイック発行モード（`--add`）: 対話的なIssue作成フロー
- パッケージ開発モード: project.md 連携
- 軽量プロジェクトモード: GitHub Project 連携

### 2. Issue 自動実装ワークフロー（5フェーズ）
- Phase 0: Issue検証・タイプ判定（ラベル/キーワード判定）
- Phase 1-5: Python ワークフロー（TDD + 品質保証）
- Phase A/C/S: Agent/Command/Skill ワークフロー

### 3. Issue ブラッシュアップ手順（8項目確認）
1. 背景・目的
2. 実装スコープ
3. 連携・依存関係
4. 優先度・期限
5. ユースケース
6. 受け入れ条件詳細
7. 実装時の注意点
8. 関連 Issue

### 4. コメント同期フロー
- comment-analyzer によるコメント解析
- 確信度ベース確認（HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW）
- task-decomposer による同期実行
- 競合解決ルール

## テストプラン

- [x] guide.md の構文が正しいことを確認
- [x] 全4つの受け入れ条件が満たされていることを確認

Fixes #617

author: davidsnam-intel
body:
### Issue:
 - MVN execution on Intel GPU shows non-deterministic results for blocked layouts (e.g. bs_fs_yx_bsv32_fsv32) even with identical inputs.
 - This PR addresses a missing work-group level synchronization when reusing local (SLM) memory across consecutive reductions inside a single kernel.

### Symptom:
- MVN output becomes randomly corrupted on certain (batch, feature) tiles.
- The corruption occurs with identical inputs, varies from run to run, looks like value collapse rather than small numerical drift.
- The issue is observed when local memory, `slm_acc`, is shared between mean and variance reductions.

### Root cause:
- The root cause is missing synchronization when reusing the same local (SLM) buffer for two consecutive reductions (`reduce_mean` → `reduce_inverse_variance`) inside the `mvn_mean_var_bsv32` kernel.
- Although `reduce_*` functions contain internal barriers, those barriers only guarantee correctness inside a single reduction.
- They do not guarantee that all sub-groups have completed reading the broadcasted result after the function returns.
- This leads to corrupted mean or variance, undefined behavior, non-deterministic results.

### How to fix:
- Use separate local variables for each `reduce_mean` and `reduce_inverse_variance`.


### Tickets:
 - CVS-115729

### Motivation

- Provide a unified, file-backed framework to collect, persist, append and archive TuShare historical data by stock and by trade-date to support downstream analysis and batch daily archiving.

author: charlesvien
body:
On the reliability front: I'm not as worried about the bugs as I am worried about our ability to ship the fixes. This is why I covered the auto updater in tests and tried to make that as durable and fault tolerant as possible. In pursuit of that we had an incident today where we released a build that failed store migrations and would not open. In a production scenario this would of left users with no option but to manually reinstall which is bad.

To fix this I implemented experimental support for Playwright e2e integration tests and added some basic happy path tests to it to ensure we don't release a broken build. @k11kirky please keep in mind we need to set the test.yml workflow as a required successful status check on this repo to ensure nothing broken can be merged.

**Contents:**
- Setup of Playwright test framework with custom Electron fixtures
- Basic smoke tests to verify app launch and stability
- Tests for main process functionality and tRPC IPC bridge
- Visual stability tests to detect UI flickering
- GitHub Actions workflow integration for running tests on macOS

**Note:** I set the concurrency to one now due to the single instance app lock logic we have, as the test suite grows we can modify it later to run integration tests in parallel.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a stable, single-process biometrics snapshot to the Hub so the UI always receives a consistent `biometrics` payload even when telemetry is quiet. 
- Surface biometrics in the WebSocket stream and UI so the visualizer and biometrics panel update independently of chat traffic. 
- Polish the Hub UI layout and branding by equalizing left/right column heights, making the EKG panel flex, replacing the mic emoji with an SVG, and correcting the visualizer title to `Oríon’s Voice`.

### Description
- Add `services/orion-hub/scripts/biometrics_cache.py` implementing `BiometricsCache` that subscribes to `orion:biometrics:*` channels, aggregates per-node state, computes composites/trends/constraint heuristics, and exposes `get_snapshot()` with stable defaults. 
- Wire the cache into the Hub lifecycle by instantiating and starting it in `services/orion-hub/scripts/main.py` and stopping it on shutdown. 
- Enrich WebSocket payloads by adding `_with_biometrics` and sending `biometrics` in all outgoing WS messages, add a periodic `biometrics_heartbeat`, and pass the cache into `websocket_endpoint` in `services/orion-hub/scripts/websocket_handler.py`. 
- Add default/merged biometrics handling in `services/orion-cortex-exec/app/executor.py` via `_default_biometrics_context` and improved parsing of state RPC replies. 
- Update settings and environment wiring by adding biometrics settings to `services/orion-hub/app/settings.py`, `services/orion-hub/.env_example`, and the `services/orion-hub/docker-compose.yml` environment block to ensure variables are present and propagated. 
- Implement the UI panel and client rendering: add biometrics UI elements and node selector in `services/orion-hub/templates/index.html`, implement client-side rendering and interaction in `services/orion-hub/static/js/app.js` (preserve paragraph breaks, Shift+Enter handling, render biometrics values/trends, and wire incoming `biometrics` payloads to the panel), and bump cache-busting asset versions for `style.css` and `app.js`. 
- Add a smoke test doc `services/orion-hub/scripts/smoke_biometrics_ws.md` describing how to validate the biometrics panel and bus traffic. 
- UI tweaks: equalize left/right column heights by setting matching `h-[44rem] min-h-0` on columns and make the EKG iframe flex within the left column, replace the mic emoji with an inline SVG, and correct the visualizer label to `Oríon’s Voice` in `templates/index.html`.

### Testing
- Launched a local static server with `python -m http.server 8000` in `services/orion-hub` and ran a Playwright script that opened `templates/index.html`; the script completed successfully and produced the screenshot artifact `artifacts/hub-ui-equal-height-v2.png`. 
- Manually verified the UI changes in the screenshot: equal-height columns, EKG panel flex behavior, updated mic SVG, and the `Oríon’s Voice` header. 
- No unit tests were added and no automated unit/integration test suite was executed beyond the Playwright screenshot check.

body:
This pull request updates the `Dockerfile` to modernize and streamline the PHP build environment, primarily by switching to a new PHP extension installation method and cleaning up package dependencies. The most important changes are grouped below:

## Build process modernization

* Replaces manual PHP extension installation with the `install-php-extensions` script, downloaded directly from its GitHub release. This simplifies and standardizes extension installation.
* Removes manual download and build steps for the `amqp` PHP extension, as it is now handled by the new installer script.

## Dependency management updates

* Cleans up and updates the list of system dependencies, removing unnecessary libraries and adding only those required for GD and IMAP PHP extensions.

## Version update

* Updates the default `MAUTIC_VERSION` build argument from `6.x-dev` to `7.x-dev` to target the latest version of Mautic.

## Testing
You can build the image using:

```
docker buildx build --build-arg FLAVOUR=apache --build-arg BASE_TAG=8.3-apache-bookworm --build-arg MAUTIC_VERSION=6.0.6 -t mautic/mautic:6-apache .
```

The scraper was returning "No prices available" because regex patterns required exact text sequences (`ج.م بيع`) that no longer consistently appear in the website HTML.

- **Relaxed regex patterns** from `r'عيار 24\s*([\d,\.]+)\s*ج\.م\s*بيع'` to `r'عيار\s*24[^\d]*([\d,\.]+)'`

  - Matches first number after karat label regardless of separator characters
  - Applied to all 7 price patterns (24K, 22K, 21K, 18K, 14K, gold pound, ounce)

# Now matches all these variations:
"عيار 24 3500 ج.م بيع"    # Old format (still works)

💡 **What:** This optimization caches the compiled LangGraph `StateGraph` at module load time.
🎯 **Why:** Previously, the graph was recompiled on every single API call to `/api/sre-loop`, causing unnecessary CPU overhead and slowing down the response time.
📊 **Impact:** Reduces the latency of the `/api/sre-loop` endpoint by eliminating redundant graph compilation. The performance improvement is most significant on the first call after startup, but it benefits every subsequent call by reusing the pre-compiled graph.
🔬 **Measurement:** The optimization can be verified by observing the server logs at startup. The message "⚡ Bolt: Compiling SRE graph once at startup..." will appear only once, confirming that the expensive compilation is no longer happening on each request.

author: copilot
body:
Safe outputs execute async in a separate job, so agents calling `create_project` never receive the project URL needed for subsequent `update_project` calls. This broke campaign generation workflows where field creation requires the project URL.

## Changes

**MCP server handler** (`safe_outputs_handlers.cjs`)
- New `createProjectHandler` auto-generates temporary ID if not provided
- Returns `{result: "success", temporary_id: "aw_...", project: "#aw_..."}` to agent

**Tool schemas** (`safe_outputs_tools.json`)
- Added optional `temporary_id` field to `create_project`
- Updated `update_project.project` pattern to accept temporary IDs: `^(https://github\.com/...|\#?aw_[0-9a-f]{12})$`

**Project handler manager** (`safe_output_project_handler_manager.cjs`)
- Builds temporary ID → URL map as messages process
- Stores mapping after successful `create_project`: `map.set(temp_id, projectUrl)`
- Passes map to subsequent handlers

**update_project handler** (`update_project.cjs`)
- Resolves temporary IDs to actual URLs before processing
- Supports both `#aw_abc123def456` and `aw_abc123def456` formats

## Usage

```javascript
// Agent workflow (automatic)
create_project({title: "Campaign"})
// Returns: {result: "success", temporary_id: "aw_abc123def456", project: "#aw_abc123def456"}

update_project({
  project: "#aw_abc123def456",  // Resolved during safe_outputs job
  operation: "create_fields"
})
```

Pattern matches existing issue temporary ID system (`temporary_id.cjs`).

author: simhacker
body:
# 🎬 THE HEIST: MINE → OURS

## The Premise

What if you could run four parallel narrative timelines simultaneously, generate 32+ images that maintain visual coherence across all of them, and have the images *write their own dialogue*?

This PR is proof that you can.

---

## 📊 Harper's Numbers

| Metric | Count |
|--------|-------|
| **Files Changed** | 305 |
| **Lines Added** | 31,765 |
| **Images Generated** | 32+ |
| **Image Mining Passes** | 40+ |
| **Slideshows Created** | 6 |
| **Cross-References Updated** | 150+ |
| **Self-Captioning Images** | 15+ |
| **Treasure Valued** | $1,619,764,800 |
| **Alliances Formed** | 1 |

---

## 🎭 The Four Timelines

### Timeline A: The Heist (10 frames)
Surveillance footage from Camera ACM1 in the Leela Manufacturing lobby, documenting a break-in at ACME Surplus. Features Chekhov's Tunnel—introduced in Frame 02, *fired* in Frame 07.

### Timeline B: Donna's Selfies (11 images)
Real-time documentation from inside the ACME control room. Donna posts to all platforms simultaneously. Mushroom pins multiply with each triumph. Pink heart glasses appear at Selfie 04.

### Timeline C: The Pub (4 scenes)
Post-heist fellowship at The Neverending Arms (which renamed itself to THE HOPPY HARE in the generated images). Scott McCloud masking. The silence that says everything.

### Timeline D: Don's MINE to OURS Arc (7 selfies)
```
MINE ──────────────────────────→ OURS

Identity → Play → Treasure → Rival → Standoff → Mirror → Alliance
```

---

## 🧪 What We Demonstrated

### 1. YES AND as Engineering Principle

Every emergent element was accepted as canon:
- Glitchy Frame 01 → Camera interference (kept both versions)
- Tunnel multiplication → Spatial anomaly in ACME basement
- Self-captioning images → Character voices emerging from the model
- "SMASH THE PATRIARCHY... WITH CONFETTI" → The protest sign improved itself
- Missing text in Frame 06 → Deliberate silence (MORE powerful)

### 2. The Coherence Engine

Visual consistency across 32+ images:
- Don's tie-dye hoodie (always present, even post-transformation)
- Donna's pink glasses (from Selfie 04 onward, continuous)
- Tunnel evolution (checkered → orange → spiral → vortex)
- Character labels emerged and persisted

### 3. Files as State

The MOOLLM principle proven at scale:
- Moving `heist-footage/` to `leela-manufacturing/lobby/` = footage lives where camera lives
- Moving `the-neverending-arms/` to `pub/photos/post-heist-fellowship/` = photos belong in pub
- Timestamps in filenames = temporal sorting
- 150+ cross-references maintained through reorganization

### 4. Image Mining (The MINE Pun)

```yaml
# MINE (verb): Extract semantic treasure from pixels
# MINE (possessive): IT'S ALL MINE!!! (Daffy Duck energy)
# image-mine: Both simultaneously
```

---

## 🏗️ New Infrastructure

### Slideshow Network
```
              SLIDESHOW-INDEX
                    │
                    ▼
         ┌─── MASTER-SYNTHESIS ───┐
         │                        │
   ┌─────┼────────┬──────────┼─────────┐
   ▼     ▼        ▼          ▼         ▼
RICHARD HEIST ←→ DONNA    PUB  ←→   DON
```

Every slideshow links to every related slideshow. Enter anywhere, navigate everywhere.

### README Front Pages
Every directory with a SLIDESHOW.md now has a README.md that:
- Introduces content (no images on front page)
- Lists characters and key moments
- Links to slideshow for visual journey

---

## 💎 Key Moments

1. **The Pledge** — Don accepts his rabbit transformation
2. **Punk-Hippie Synthesis** — "They ARE delightfully compatible"
3. **Operation Inflation** — Play as protest (inflatable bunny costume)
4. **The Treasure Vault** — $1.6B in assets, Daffy Duck energy
5. **Donna Arrives** — "OH NO!" vs "MINE! MINE!"
6. **The Realization** — No dialogue. Silence is the point.
7. **The OURS Accord** — Reluctant partnership sealed

---

## 🎬 The Story Arc

```
HEIST → CHAOS → TRANSFORMATION → FELLOWSHIP → CONFRONTATION → ALLIANCE

Don started human.
Don ended rabbit.
Don ended PARTNER.
```

---

## 📝 Session Documentation

- `sessions/2026-01-23-05-30-00-deep-cursor-mirror-reflection.md` — This analysis
- `sessions/2026-01-23-mine-to-ours-treasure-arc.md` — Full arc narrative
- `sessions/2026-01-23-the-pledge.md` — Don's acceptance

---

## The Quote

> *"MINE is lonely. OURS is... complicated. But complicated can be better."*

---

🐰🤝🍄

*The frob adjusts itself — and then DOCUMENTS itself.*

body:
RISK: HIGH. Requires explicit operator approval.

## Summary
Adds a deterministic replay compare report generator (COMPARE_JSON) via a new `compare` CLI subcommand. It reads a replay bundle, optionally integrates DataRefs resolution, runs replay and (optionally) output invariant checks, and emits a canonical JSON report for CI/ops consumption.

## Key behavior
- New CLI subcommand: compare
- Optional DataRefs resolve: best_effort or strict; existing resolution report is respected if present
- Default artifact: meta/compare_report.json
- Deterministic output: canonical JSON (sorted keys), LF-only, no wall-clock (derived from manifest or overridden via --generated-at-utc)

## Exit codes (explicit)
- 0: PASS
- 2: contract/schema violation
- 3: hash mismatch (bundle or datarefs sha256_hint mismatch in strict)
- 4: replay mismatch (output invariant failure when --check-outputs enabled)
- 6: missing required dataref (strict)
- 5: unexpected exception

## CLI (examples)
```bash
python3 scripts/execution/pt_replay_pack.py compare --bundle <BUNDLE_DIR> --generated-at-utc <ISO8601>
python3 scripts/execution/pt_replay_pack.py compare --bundle <BUNDLE_DIR> --check-outputs --generated-at-utc <ISO8601>
python3 scripts/execution/pt_replay_pack.py compare --bundle <BUNDLE_DIR> --resolve-datarefs best_effort --cache-root <CACHE_ROOT> --generated-at-utc <ISO8601>
python3 scripts/execution/pt_replay_pack.py compare --bundle <BUNDLE_DIR> --resolve-datarefs strict --cache-root <CACHE_ROOT> --generated-at-utc <ISO8601>
```

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Adds a deterministic compare report generator for replay bundles.
> 
> - New `compare` CLI subcommand with `--check-outputs`, `--resolve-datarefs {best_effort|strict}`, `--cache-root`, `--generated-at-utc`, and `--out`
> - Implements `generate_compare_report` to validate bundle, optionally resolve/embed DataRefs, replay events, compute invariants (`fills`, `positions`) and diffs, and emit canonical JSON at `meta/compare_report.json`
> - Deterministic behavior: canonical JSON, LF-only, no wall-clock (timestamp derived or overridden)
> - Clear exit codes: 0 OK, 2 contract/schema, 3 hash mismatch, 4 replay mismatch, 6 missing required dataref, 5 unexpected
> - Docs updated (execution and runbook) with usage/examples; comprehensive tests added for pass/fail cases, datarefs modes, and byte-for-byte determinism

author: nickm538
body:
This commit addresses two issues identified in code review:
1.  A race condition in the `BiologistAgent`'s Sentinel Hub token refresh logic. An `asyncio.Lock` has been added to ensure that the token refresh process is thread-safe, preventing multiple concurrent requests from attempting to refresh the token simultaneously.
2.  The use of `-dev` packages in the runtime stage of the `server/Dockerfile`. The Dockerfile has been updated to use the specific runtime libraries (`libhdf5-103`, `libnetcdf19`) instead of the larger development packages, which reduces the final image size and improves security.

author: dlipicar
body:
Integrate tokenbalances and tokenhistoricalownership services into wallet, replacing reader.go with cleaner event-driven architecture. Also refactor token manager to remove balance persistence responsibilities.

Token Manager Changes:
- Add publisher for token list change notifications
- Add EventTokenListUpdated event type
- Remove balance caching (GetCachedBalances, CacheBalances)
- Remove MarkAsPreviouslyOwnedToken (moved to tokenhistoricalownership)
- Remove internal balance storage
- Add HistoricallyOwnedTokensProvider interface
- Delete balance_persistence.go and related files

Service Integration:
- Delete reader.go and related test files
- Instantiate tokenBalancesService in wallet service
- Instantiate tokenHistoricalOwnershipService in wallet service
- Wire up service dependencies and event publishers
- Update API to use tokenBalancesService instead of reader
- Add new API endpoint GetAllBalances() with state information
- Add api_token_balances_test.go
- Update token manager initialization to use new services
- Connect tokenHistoricalOwnership to activity, balances, and transfers

API Changes:
- Replace GetCachedWalletBalances with GetAllBalances
- GetAllBalances returns balances with state (Idle/Updating/Error)
- Each balance includes block number, block hash, and fetch timestamp

Integration Points:
- tokenBalancesService subscribes to multistandardbalance events
- tokenHistoricalOwnershipService subscribes to:
  - Activity events (via activityfetcher)
  - Balance change events (via tokenBalancesService)
  - Transfer events (via transferdetector)
- Token manager uses historicallyOwnedTokensProvider interface

body:
Website lacked professional polish - basic CSS with minimal visual hierarchy, no animations, standard shadows. Enhanced to align with modern corporate design standards (www.obsglobal.com aesthetic).

## Changes

### Typography & Performance
- Added Google Fonts (Inter/Poppins) via HTML `<link>` with preconnect (not CSS `@import`) for faster loading
- Enhanced font hierarchy: 4rem headlines with -0.02em letter-spacing, 1.7 line-height
- Enabled font-smoothing for crisp rendering

### Visual Design
- Implemented multi-stop gradients (135deg) with radial overlays in hero sections
- Enhanced shadows: `0 1px 3px` base → `0 12px 24px` on hover with 8px translateY
- Feature icons with gradient backgrounds and scale transforms on hover
- Cards with animated top border gradient on hover

### Interactive Elements
- Navigation: glassmorphism (`backdrop-filter: blur(10px)`) with animated underline hover states
- Buttons: gradient backgrounds with shimmer effect using pseudo-element transforms
- All transitions use `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` for professional feel

### Accessibility & Animations
- Entrance animations (fadeInUp, staggered grid delays) wrapped in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`
- Removed overly aggressive universal selector with `!important` flags
- Maintained semantic HTML and focus states

### Responsive Design
- Enhanced mobile breakpoint (768px) with adjusted typography scale

issue：https://github.com/matrixorigin/matrixone/issues/11171
原因： ODBC 在连接初始化阶段访问 @@server_id，而 MatrixOne 没定义该系统变量，触发 “system variable does not exist”。
方案是补 server_id 系统变量定义并加测试验证：
代码：variables.go 新增 server_id（global、只读、int64、默认 0）。
测试：system_variables.sql / .result 增加 SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'server_id' 和 SELECT @@server_id

issue：https://github.com/matrixorigin/matrixone/issues/14490
14490的里面说的原生tpcc报错没能复现出来,没发现一样的问题
1.HyBench Duplicate entry '0' for key 'id'
原因：HyBench 的 SQL 显式插入 id=0，MySQL 默认 sql_mode 下应视为 NULL 并触发自增；MO 之前把 0 当作真实值写入，导致重复键。
修复：在 auto_increment 处理阶段，当 sql_mode 不含 NO_AUTO_VALUE_ON_ZERO 时，将自增列中值为 0 的行视作 NULL，让其走自增逻辑。
2.TPC‑C invalid argument operator in, bad value [TUPLE TUPLE]
原因：(a,b) IN ((1,2),(3,4)) 这类 tuple IN 被当成普通标量 IN 去匹配函数重载，导致类型成了 TUPLE IN TUPLE，没有对应 operator overload。
修复：在 binder 层识别左侧为 tuple 的 IN/NOT IN，强制走 tuple 处理路径（handleTupleIn），避免走标量函数匹配。

author: marceloteck
body:
### Motivation
- Improve generation quality by protecting learned cores and penalizing games that miss critical nucleus blocks (RAN) and enable compacting larger candidate games into smaller final sizes while preserving structure. 
- Increase strategy diversity by adding parametrizable heuristic brains and structural brains to broaden candidate generation. 
- Provide evaluation, reporting and an interactive dashboard to measure, operate and automate large-scale evaluation and training. 
- Consolidate runnable project commands in a single reference so users can run setup, training, generation, status and dashboard tasks easily from the project root.

### Description
- Implemented RAN/core protection and compaction in `START/gerar_proximo_concurso.py` via `build_core_c`, `ran_penalty` and `compact_game`, plus new CLI flags such as `--base-size`, `--ran-strict`, `--ensemble-bonus`, `--exploration-rate` and `--max-brain-share` and options for `--qtd-strong` and `--second-size`/`--second-qtd`.
- Extended `BrainHub` (`training/core/brain_hub.py`) to accept `exploration_rate` and `max_brain_share`, normalize per-brain scores, apply a meta-weight from past performance, inject exploration noise, and diversify selection with per-brain share limits and adaptive similarity thresholds.
- Added new brains: structural protections `training/brains/structural/core_protect_brain.py` and `training/brains/structural/anti_absence_brain.py`, plus a family of heuristic brains in `training/brains/heuristic/heuristic_brains.py` with registration helpers in `training/brains/heuristic/__init__.py` and wiring into `training/trainer_v2.py` and `START/gerar_proximo_concurso.py`.
- Added evaluation and reporting tooling: `scripts/avaliar_desempenho.py`, `scripts/gerar_dashboard_html.py`, a Flask dashboard at `src/web_dashboard.py` with template `src/templates/dashboard.html`, `start_dashboard.bat`, and a GitHub Actions workflow `/.github/workflows/relatorio_avaliacao.yml` to run batch evaluations and upload artifacts.
- Added a command reference file `COMANDOS.md` at repository root that lists all runnable commands and .bat shortcuts for setup, DB maintenance, training, generation, status, backtests, evaluation and dashboard operations.

### Testing
- No automated tests or CI jobs were executed for these changes. 
- Changes are primarily new modules, CLI flags and documentation; manual runtime validation is recommended (e.g. `python START/gerar_proximo_concurso.py`, `python -m training.trainer_v2`, `python scripts/avaliar_desempenho.py`, and `python -m src.web_dashboard`).
- The addition of `COMANDOS.md` is documentation-only and was committed without running test suites.

body:
### Motivation
- Preserve measurement files and 3/4-position switch selections when exporting/importing reports so measurement data can be re-rendered after sharing and switch states restored. 
- Persist amplifier adjustment snapshots inside exports so exported artifacts and generated PDF reflect current amplifier settings. 
- Move UI coloring to theme-aware tokens and adapt measurement/amplifier UIs to MaterialTheme so tables, amplifier cards and charts work across light/dark modes. 
- Fix a Kotlin type inference error when building measurement tables for the PDF export to avoid a runtime/compile error at the table emission site.

### Description
- Add measurement export/import support: implement `collectMeasurementFiles`, `ExportMeasurementFile` (base64 payload), and write/read measurement files during `exportToJSON`/`exportToZIP` and `importFromJSON`/`importFromZip` with Base64 encoding/decoding and proper folder placement. 
- Add switch selection persistence: introduce `switchPrefs`, `collectSwitchSelections` and `applySwitchSelections`, include `switchSelections` in `ExportData`/`ExportDataV2`, and restore them on import. 
- Persist amplifier adjustments inside exports and restore them on import by adding `adjustments` to `ExportData`/`ExportDataV2` and calling `upsertAmplifierAdjustment` during import. 
- Enhance PDF generation in `ExportManager.exportToPDF` to include a "Carga de Mediciones" section that prints DOCSIS and Channel Expert tables derived from `verifyMeasurementFiles`, and fix typing by adding explicit row type annotations (`List<List<Pair<String, com.itextpdf.kernel.colors.Color?>>>`) for `pilotRows` and `digitalRows` to avoid Kotlin inference errors. 
- Update ZIP export to copy measurement folders for both RX and module (for `NODE` assets) and include `report.json` with image refs, adjustments and switch selections. 
- Theme and UI changes: add Outlook-inspired color tokens in `ui/theme/Color.kt` and map them in `ui/theme/Theme.kt`, add `SuccessGreen`; convert hard-coded colors in `AmplifierAdjustmentCard` to `MaterialTheme.colorScheme` via small `@Composable` helpers and use `SuccessGreen` for OK deltas; refactor measurement UI components (`MeasurementTableCard`, `MeasurementTableRow`) to accept `containerColor`, `headerColor`, `borderColor`, and `dividerColor`, and update usages in `AddAssetScreen` to pass themed colors while replacing local `anomalyColor` with `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error`.

author: jython1415
body:
## Summary

Adds comprehensive test coverage for 6 previously untested hooks, bringing total test coverage from **14% (1/7 hooks)** to **100% (7/7 hooks)**.

This PR also **refactors the test infrastructure** to follow Python ecosystem best practices by migrating from PEP 723 inline dependencies to `pyproject.toml` dependency groups.

---

## Part 1: Comprehensive Test Coverage

### New Test Files (253 tests total)

1. **test_normalize_line_endings.py** (32 tests)
   - CRLF/CR/LF normalization testing
   - Edge cases (binary content, empty files, whitespace)
   - Real-world scenarios (Python, JSON, Markdown, shell scripts)
   
2. **test_prefer_modern_tools.py** (58 tests)
   - fd/rg suggestion detection
   - Adaptive testing (skips tests when tools not installed)
   - Edge cases (quoted strings, environment variables, filenames)
   
3. **test_auto_unsandbox_pbcopy.py** (39 tests)
   - pbcopy detection and auto-approval
   - Sandbox disabling verification
   - Complex pipe patterns and real-world scenarios
   
4. **test_gh_fallback_helper.py** (36 tests)
   - GitHub CLI fallback detection
   - GITHUB_TOKEN environment handling
   - API guidance and curl examples
   
5. **test_gpg_signing_helper.py** (40 tests)
   - GPG signing error detection
   - Multiple error patterns (failed to sign, agent issues)
   - PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure handling
   
6. **test_detect_heredoc_errors.py** (48 tests)
   - Heredoc error detection and workarounds
   - Multiple error field locations
   - Comprehensive guidance testing

---

## Part 2: Test Infrastructure Refactor

### What Changed

**Before:** Each test file used PEP 723 inline dependencies
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# /// script
# dependencies = ["pytest>=7.0.0"]
# ///
```

**After:** Centralized dependency management in `pyproject.toml`
```toml
[dependency-groups]
dev = ["pytest>=7.0.0"]
```

### Why This Matters

After comprehensive research of PEP 723, PEP 735, and modern Python tooling practices, we discovered that **using PEP 723 for test files is an anti-pattern**.

**Key findings:**
- ❌ PEP 723 is designed for standalone production scripts, not development infrastructure
- ❌ Tests are tooling (not deliverables) and should use standard dependency management
- ❌ Duplicating `pytest>=7.0.0` across 7 files violates DRY principle
- ❌ No lock file support = unreproducible test environments
- ❌ Can't run standard `pytest` discovery workflows

**The Solution:**
- ✅ Production hooks continue using PEP 723 (appropriate for standalone scripts)
- ✅ Tests use `pyproject.toml` with PEP 735 dependency groups (standard practice)
- ✅ Creates semantic separation: production code vs. development tooling
- ✅ Enables `uv run pytest` for standard testing workflow
- ✅ Lock file (`uv.lock`) ensures reproducible builds
- ✅ Single source of truth for test dependencies

### Research Sources

- [PEP 723 – Inline script metadata](https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/)
- [PEP 735 – Dependency Groups in pyproject.toml](https://peps.python.org/pep-0735/)
- [uv Issue #9061 – Testing with PEP 723](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/9061)
- [Python Developer Tooling Handbook – PEP 723](https://pydevtools.com/handbook/explanation/what-is-pep-723/)
- [Simon Willison's TIL – Dependency groups and uv](https://til.simonwillison.net/uv/dependency-groups)

---

## Test Results

```
============================= test session starts ==============================
collected 283 items

269 passed, 14 skipped in 35.13s
```

- **269 tests passed** ✅
- **14 tests skipped** (fd not installed - expected, rg is available)
- **0 failures** ✅

---

## Running Tests

**New simplified workflow:**
```bash
uv run pytest              # Run all tests
uv run pytest -v           # Verbose output  
uv run pytest hooks/tests/test_*.py  # Run specific tests
```

**Old workflow (deprecated):**
```bash
# No longer needed - PEP 723 headers removed
uv run --script hooks/tests/test_*.py
```

---

## Quality Standards

All tests follow the established pattern from `test_detect_cd_pattern.py`:

- ✅ Comprehensive edge case coverage
- ✅ Clear, descriptive test names
- ✅ Comprehensive docstrings
- ✅ Error handling tests
- ✅ JSON output validation
- ✅ Helper functions for running hooks

---

## Benefits

1. **100% Test Coverage**: All hooks now have comprehensive regression protection
2. **Best Practices**: Tests follow modern Python ecosystem standards (PEP 735)
3. **Reproducible Builds**: Lock file ensures consistent test environments
4. **Single Source of Truth**: One place to manage test dependencies
5. **Standard Workflow**: Use industry-standard `uv run pytest` command
6. **Easy Maintenance**: Update pytest once instead of in 7 files
7. **Semantic Architecture**: Clear separation between production code (PEP 723) and tooling (pyproject.toml)

---

## Files Changed

**New files:**
- `pyproject.toml` – Project metadata and dependency groups
- `uv.lock` – Dependency lock file for reproducibility
- `hooks/tests/test_*.py` (6 new test files)

**Modified files:**
- `hooks/tests/test_*.py` (7 files) – Removed PEP 723 headers, updated docstrings

**Total changes:** +2,988 lines across 9 files

---

## Next Steps

With 100% test coverage and proper infrastructure in place, the repository is ready to:
- ✅ Implement Issue #3 (uv run enforcement hook)
- ✅ Implement Issue #4 (temp file location hook)
- ✅ Implement Issue #5 (emoji usage linter)
- ✅ Safely refactor existing hooks with confidence

author: konard
body:
## Summary
Fixes the frag grenade's HE (High Explosive) damage which was not working correctly. Enemies within the blast zone were not being killed by the shockwave.

## Root Cause

The `explosion_damage` value in `scenes/projectiles/FragGrenade.tscn` was incorrectly set to `2` instead of `99`:

```ini
# Before (incorrect):
explosion_damage = 2

# After (correct):
explosion_damage = 99
```

This value overrides the default `explosion_damage = 99` defined in the script `scripts/projectiles/frag_grenade.gd`.

### Evidence from Logs

From the game log provided in the issue:

```
[07:21:53] [ENEMY] [Enemy3] Hit taken, health: 2/3
[07:21:53] [ENEMY] [Enemy3] Hit taken, health: 1/3
[07:21:53] [INFO] [FragGrenade] Applied 2 HE damage to enemy at distance 226.7
```

The log showed only 2 damage was applied (reducing Enemy3's health from 3 to 1), when it should have been 99 damage (instantly killing the enemy).

## Changes

### `scenes/projectiles/FragGrenade.tscn`
- Changed `explosion_damage` from `2` to `99` (main fix)
- Changed `effect_radius` from `250.0` to `225.0` (per requirement: ~450 diameter zone)

### `scripts/projectiles/frag_grenade.gd`
- Updated default `effect_radius` from `250.0` to `225.0` for consistency
- Updated comment to reflect the user requirement

### Documentation
- Added `docs/case-studies/issue-206/` with detailed root cause analysis and game log

## Shockwave Physics

The code already correctly implements physics-based shockwave propagation:
- Uses raycast line-of-sight check (`_has_line_of_sight_to()`)
- Checks for obstacles (walls) with `collision_mask = 4`
- Only applies damage if there's clear line of sight (no walls blocking)

This means the shockwave is correctly blocked by walls.

## Test Plan

- [ ] Throw frag grenade near enemies in open area - should instantly kill all enemies within 225px radius
- [ ] Throw frag grenade near enemies behind a wall - wall should block shockwave damage
- [ ] Verify shrapnel continues to work (4 pieces, ricochet, 1 damage each)

Fixes #206

author: siddartha2020t
body:
During evaluation runs, the agent was failing with HTTP 413 errors when
the request payload exceeded API size limits. The existing error handling
only checked for the "25000000" byte limit string, but did not catch:
- HTTP 413 status code responses
- "request_too_large" error messages
- "maximum size" validation errors

This caused the agent to crash instead of gracefully reducing image count
and retrying the request.

Changes:
- Extended size error detection to include "413", "request_too_large",
  and "maximum size" patterns
- Applied fix to both primary API retry loop and backup API fallback
- Agent now automatically halves image count on any size-related error
  and retries, keeping at least 1 image
-  added tasks in the examples.

body:
## Summary

Fixes the critical bug where users cannot scroll on the main transactions page and can only see ~3 transactions.

## Root Cause

In CSS flexbox, elements with `flex-1` default to `min-height: auto`, which prevents them from shrinking below their content size. This breaks `overflow-y-auto` scrolling.

## Fix

Added `min-h-0` class to the transactions list container:

```diff
- <div className="flex-1 overflow-y-auto p-6 max-w-7xl mx-auto w-full">
+ <div className="flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto p-6 max-w-7xl mx-auto w-full">
```

- `POST /tracks/{id}/share` - creates tracked share link, returns URL with `?ref=` code
- `POST /tracks/{id}/ref/{code}/click` - records visit (called on page load)
- `GET /tracks/me/shares` - paginated stats: who visited, who played, how many times

**extended playback** (`backend/src/backend/api/tracks/playback.py`)
- play endpoint now accepts optional `ref` param to record play events

</details>

<details>
<summary>frontend changes</summary>

**player state** (`frontend/src/lib/player.svelte.ts`)
- tracks current `ref` code, includes in play count POST body
- clears ref when track changes

**track page** (`frontend/src/routes/track/[id]/+page.svelte`)
- captures `?ref=` param on load, fires click event to backend
- stores ref in player state for play attribution

**share button** (`frontend/src/lib/components/ShareButton.svelte`)
- authenticated users get tracked links via `POST /tracks/{id}/share`
- unauthenticated users get plain URLs (no tracking)

**portal** (`frontend/src/routes/portal/+page.svelte`)
- share stats section with expandable cards per share link
- shows visitors (who clicked) and listeners (who played) with avatar circles
- displays individual interaction counts per user

</details>

<details>
<summary>design decisions</summary>

- **unique users, not total events**: headline shows "2 visitors" meaning 2 different people, not 5 total clicks. matches "read receipt" mental model - you want to know *who* clicked, not how many times
- **self-clicks skipped**: clicking your own share link doesn't record (avoids inflating stats)
- **anonymous tracking**: anonymous visits/plays increment counts but don't reveal identity
- **8-char codes**: `secrets.token_urlsafe(6)` gives 48 bits of entropy (~281 trillion possibilities), collision retry handles edge cases

</details>

author: copilot
body:
Implements a reusable `RangeSliderWidget` for filtering map features by numeric or ISO8601 timestamp ranges, with non-destructive hide/show semantics.

## Components

**RangeSliderWidget** (`pyopenlayersqt/range_slider.py`)
- **Single slider with two draggable handles** (left handle for min, right handle for max)
- Custom `DualHandleSlider` widget with visual feedback and smooth drag interactions
- Configurable min/max/step for numeric ranges
- ISO8601 timestamp mode: maps sorted unique timestamps to slider indices
- Emits `rangeChanged(min_value, max_value)` signal
- Compact UI with horizontal track and highlighted selection range

**Layer Filtering API** (`pyopenlayersqt/layers.py`)
- `hide_features(ids)`, `show_features(ids)`, `show_all_features()` on FastPointsLayer/FastGeoPointsLayer
- Features hidden (not deleted) - preserved in memory for filter state changes

**Table Row Hiding** (`pyopenlayersqt/features_table.py`)
- `hide_rows_by_keys()`, `show_rows_by_keys()`, `show_all_rows()` 
- Uses `QTableView.setRowHidden()` for efficient hiding without proxy model

**JavaScript Bridge** (`pyopenlayersqt/resources/ol_bridge.js`)
- Added `hidden[]` array alongside `deleted[]` in fast layer entries
- Rendering and hit-detection skip `hidden` features
- Commands: `fast_points.hide_ids`, `fast_points.show_ids`, `fast_points.show_all` (+ geopoints equivalents)

## Usage

```python
from pyopenlayersqt import RangeSliderWidget

# Numeric filtering - single slider with two handles
slider = RangeSliderWidget(min_val=0, max_val=100, step=1, label="Value")
slider.rangeChanged.connect(lambda min_v, max_v: apply_filter(min_v, max_v))

# ISO8601 timestamp filtering (auto-converts to slider indices)
timestamps = ["2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", "2024-01-15T12:00:00Z", ...]
slider = RangeSliderWidget(values=sorted(set(timestamps)), label="Time")

# Apply filtering
layer.hide_features(hidden_ids)  # Non-destructive
layer.show_all_features()        # Reset filter
table.hide_rows_by_keys(keys)    # Sync table state
```

## UI Design

The range slider features a single horizontal track with:
- Two circular draggable handles (white with shadows)
- Blue highlighted selection range between handles
- Hover cursor feedback
- Click on track to move nearest handle
- Min and Max value labels displayed below the slider

## Example

`examples/05_range_slider_filter.py` demonstrates filtering 5,000 fast points by value and timestamp with bidirectional map/table sync.

> Requirements:
> - Implement a new RangeSliderWidget in the pyopenlayersqt package that supports setting min, max, and step size, emits signals when the range changes (min/max), and can be configured for numeric ranges.
> - Support a special case for ISO8601 string values by converting to/from numeric values for slider usage while preserving original values for filtering and display.
> - Provide filtering logic that hides (not removes) features outside the selected range. When the range expands, previously hidden features must become visible again. Filtering must work across all layer types (vector, fast points, fast geo points, etc.).
> - Integrate filtering with FeatureTableWidget so that filtering by the selected column hides features on the map; keep feature rows accessible for filtering state changes.

## Vercel Speed Insights Implementation

Successfully implemented Vercel Speed Insights for the Al Marji project, a React + Vite application.

### What Was Implemented

This implementation adds real-time performance monitoring to the application following Vercel's Speed Insights setup guide.

### Files Modified

1. **package.json**

### Implementation Details

The project is a React application using Vite as the build tool. Following Vercel's documentation for React/Vite applications, the SpeedInsights component was added to the application's entry point (index.tsx) alongside the existing Vercel Analytics component.

The component is placed in the root render tree to ensure:
- Automatic performance metrics collection across all pages and routes
- Tracking of Web Vitals (LCP, FID, CLS, etc.)
- Seamless integration with the existing Vercel Analytics setup
- Minimal performance overhead

### Why This Approach

For React applications (particularly those using modern frameworks like Vite), the `@vercel/speed-insights/react` package provides the best integration. The SpeedInsights component:
- Works as a client-side component
- Automatically injects the tracking script
- Provides zero-configuration setup
- Integrates cleanly with React's component model

This follows the same pattern as the existing `@vercel/analytics` component already in the project.

### Next Steps for Users

After deploying this version to Vercel:

1. Enable Speed Insights in the Vercel dashboard (Project → Speed Insights tab → Enable)
2. Deploy the application to Vercel using `vercel deploy` or by connecting the git repository
3. Once deployed, the tracking script will automatically appear in the page source (`/_vercel/speed-insights/script.js`)

author: copilot
body:
Implements core UI enhancement infrastructure for user preferences, data operations, and contextual assistance across the application.

## Architecture

**Three-layer approach:**
- **Managers** - State persistence (localStorage/sessionStorage/memory) and LRU cache with TTL
- **Components** - Reusable UI primitives (40+ components)
- **Constants** - Centralized help text, tooltips, messages (200+ entries)

**Key design decisions:**
- Browser storage abstraction for zero-backend persistence
- LRU eviction with per-entry TTL for caching
- Mantine v2 components for consistency with existing UI
- Type-safe APIs throughout

## Implementation

### Persistence Layer
```python
from aiml_studio.managers import BrowserPersistenceManager

persistence = BrowserPersistenceManager()
persistence.save("theme", "dark", storage_type="local")  # survives refresh
persistence.save("workflow_state", data, storage_type="session")  # tab-scoped
```

### Caching System
```python
from aiml_studio.managers import cached, cache_manager

@cached(cache_manager, ttl=3600)
def expensive_query(params):
    return database.query(params)  # cached for 1 hour
```

### UI Components
```python
from aiml_studio.components import (
    create_tooltip, create_confirm_modal, create_help_icon
)
from aiml_studio.constants_help import TOOLTIPS, FIELD_HELP

# Tooltip with constant
create_tooltip(button, label=TOOLTIPS["refresh"])

# Confirmation modal
create_confirm_modal(
    modal_id="delete-confirm",
    title="Delete Project",
    message="This action cannot be undone.",
    confirm_color="red",
)

# Form with help text
create_label_with_help("Project Name", FIELD_HELP["project_name"], required=True)
```

## Changes

### New Files (10)
- `managers/persistence_manager.py` - Browser storage abstraction
- `managers/cache_manager.py` - LRU cache with TTL
- `components/notifications.py` - Toast, alerts, bell
- `components/modals.py` - Dialogs and drawers
- `components/tooltips.py` - Help icons, popovers
- `constants_help.py` - Centralized text constants
- `callbacks/global_callbacks.py` - Preference persistence

### Modified Files
- `app.py` - Wire up managers, stores, notification provider
- `layouts/home.py` - Add tooltips to actions, help icons to sections
- `layouts/projects.py` - Add help text to forms

### Integration Status
- Home & Projects pages: Tooltips and help text applied
- Remaining pages: Infrastructure ready, incremental application

## Documentation
- API reference (28 pages)
- Quick reference guide (13 pages)
- Architecture overview (30 pages)
- Examples and best practices included

## Notes
- Zero breaking changes - all additions
- Backward compatible - existing code unaffected
- Production-ready - type-safe, error handling, statistics
- Incremental adoption - apply to pages as needed

The main focus is on removing the `writePlugin` function and related plugin-handling logic from the type node generation process, and instead consolidating plugin metadata (like `title`, `deprecated`, and custom `x-` fields) into the generated comments. This results in cleaner type node generation and a more organized approach to handling schema metadata.

**Refactoring and simplification of type node generation:**

- Removed the `writePlugin` function and all related logic from type node writers (for constant, boolean, integer, number, string, array, and tuple schemas), resulting in more straightforward and concise type node creation.   - Test files: `test_tenant_isolation.py`, `test_platform_gate.py`, `conftest.py`

No logic changes. Relationships now resolve correctly at mapper configuration time.

author: box2board
body:
### Motivation
- Make the site more visual and mobile-first by replacing busy, text-heavy recipe cards with image-forward cards and a clean, modern layout. 
- Improve on-page and technical SEO across the site (meta tags, canonical links, Open Graph/Twitter tags, sitemap, and JSON-LD) so pages are ready for organic, Discover, and Pinterest traffic. 
- Provide reliable local placeholder imagery and schema that prevent external hotlinking and improve Core Web Vitals (avoid CLS by sizing images). 

### Description
- UI: replaced vintage/worksheet-style cards with modern visual cards and a responsive grid (1–4 cols) and added subtle hover/CTA states via updates to `assets/css/styles.css` and `index.html`/`recipes/index.html` card markup. 
- Images/placeholders: added local category-based SVG placeholders in `assets/img/placeholders/` and wired lazy-loading + fixed aspect sizing for all recipe images; directory and homepage now use these placeholders when a real image is missing. 
- JS: extended `assets/js/main.js` with `placeholderMap`, `getRecipeImage`, `getRecipeFacts`, `formatLabel`, dynamic `renderRecipeCards`, `initCategoryHighlights`, and recipe-meta/schema helpers that inject/update meta tags and JSON-LD at runtime. 
- Recipe pages: upgraded detail templates to include a hero image, a structured `Recipe Facts` panel, consistent headings, improved alt text, updated schema using `@type: Recipe`, and new “You Might Also Like” visual cards (files under `recipes/*.html`). 
- SEO & site metadata: tightened title/meta-description patterns, added consistent `og:` and `twitter:` tags, added organization + website JSON-LD to main pages, and updated `sitemap.xml` to include the dynamic `recipe.html` entry without changing any existing public URLs. 
- Non-breaking: left all ad and analytics snippets intact and preserved URLs; no frameworks introduced and site remains static. 

### Testing
- Local visual smoke test: served the site with `python -m http.server` and captured a homepage screenshot using Playwright; the navigation and redesigned cards rendered and the screenshot capture succeeded. 
- No unit/integration test suite was available or run as part of this change. 
- Manual checks: verified `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt` remained present and that new placeholder assets are local (no external hotlinks).

- **Memory Optimization**: Refactored image operations to take `&DynamicImage` instead of `DynamicImage`, eliminating unnecessary full-image clones during pipeline execution.
- **Route Fix**: Updated `src/server/mod.rs` to route `GET /pipeline` to the `process_pipeline` handler, enabling URL-based processing.
- **New Feature**: Added `/info` endpoint (GET/POST) to retrieve image metadata (width, height, format, color space, etc.), matching `imaginary` capabilities.
- **New Feature**: Added `filter` parameter to `ResizeParams`, supporting `Lanczos3` (default), `Gaussian`, `Nearest`, `Triangle`, and `CatmullRom` resizing algorithms.
- **Refactoring**: Extracted common HTTP request utilities (`fetch_image_from_url`, `is_safe_ip`) to `src/http/request_utils.rs`.
- **Testing**: Updated unit tests to reflect ownership changes and verify new functionality. All 77 unit tests and 10 integration tests pass.

This PR implements memory optimizations by refactoring image operations to use references (`&DynamicImage`) instead of owned values, eliminating unnecessary clones during pipeline execution. It adds a new `/info` endpoint (supporting both GET and POST) to retrieve image metadata including dimensions, format, and color space information. The resize operation now supports configurable filter algorithms (`Lanczos3`, `Gaussian`, `Nearest`, `Triangle`, `CatmullRom`). The PR also fixes routing by adding GET support to the `/pipeline` endpoint and extracts common HTTP utilities (`fetch_image_from_url`, `is_safe_ip`) into a reusable `request_utils` module for better code organization.

author: radiatedsaturn7
body:
### Motivation
- Make the piano-roll grid align to the selected quantize / note-length so visual grid lines match snapping and default to quarter-note spacing.
- Improve copy/cut/paste workflow by allowing the user to place a paste preview and confirm with a contextual `Paste Here` action instead of immediately pasting.
- Let users preview and download GM instruments for offline use and preload common instruments to speed up playback previews.

### Description
- Grid & controls: changed default quantize index to `0`, draw vertical grid lines at the quantize step, moved the note-length control into the grid header, and added on-canvas zoom buttons with bounds at `drawGridZoomControls` in `src/ui/MidiComposer.js`.
- Paste-preview workflow: `copySelection` still captures selection, `pasteSelection` now begins a preview (`beginPastePreview`) and shows a `Paste Here` button; `applyPastePreview` commits the notes when the user confirms; paste UI and bounds added in `drawPastePreview` and input handling updated in `handlePointerDown`/`handlePointerUp`.
- Instrument preview & download: instrument preview now loads the GM program (or drum kit) and plays a short sequence (e.g. `1 4 5 1`) with loading indicators; instrument download button added to the Instrument Settings panel and wired to a new `downloadTrackInstrument` flow in `MidiComposer`.
- SoundFont caching & preload: added `cacheInstrument`, `cacheDrumKit`, and `cacheInstrumentByName` to `src/audio/SoundfontEngine.js` which use the Cache API to fetch and store soundfont JS files; exposed `cacheGmProgram` in `src/game/Audio.js`; `MidiComposer` stores cached keys in `localStorage` and preloads a small set of default programs (`DEFAULT_PRELOAD_PROGRAMS`).
- UI/UX tweaks: simplified the header and moved the `File` button into the tab row; after applying an instrument selection the editor returns to the `grid` tab; loading/download states are shown in the instrument panel.

### Testing
- Launched the local dev server with `./run.sh` and opened the app in a headless browser via a Playwright script that navigated to `index.html` and captured a screenshot (`artifacts/midi-editor.png`), which completed successfully.
- Verified interactive flows manually via the screenshot run (previewed MIDI editor UI, instrument panel and grid controls rendering); no unit tests were added or modified.
