author: bryce-mcmath
body:
# Summary of Changes

This PR follows openwallet-foundation/bifold-wallet#1751 by extending the React Native 81 upgrade to our project. It includes all the same equivalent changes, plus some additional changes as we have some additional libraries that Bifold doesn't like react-native-date-picker, FCM, react-native-webrtc and others.

Further PRs will come for new architecture support and 16kb memory page size support, but those require updating or swapping out many dependencies, so to make things more piecemeal, this PR just deals with upgrading react-native and staying with the old arch.

If you don't use mise, you will need to have rbenv or an equivalent installed so you can use the correct ruby and bundler version. Both projects now use ruby 3.3.6.

Some notes I took during this upgrade:
- The new Xcode 26.2 works now
- Our TypeScript version is too far ahead of our TS + ESLint packages and as such, some TS errors aren't being caught. That should be updated in a future PR (you have probably seen the console warnings when running typechecks)
- FCM has deprecated most of the API we are using, the update to the new API is fairly straight forward, but should be done before the next major version bump.
- We shouldn't import the entirety of lodash to use a single method, we should import just that method only for treeshaking and bundle size benefits.
- Our push notification permissions issue workaround is no longer needed, that stuff can be cleaned up now when there is time
- iOS build times take longer but this can be optimized by enabling ccache in your Podfile (don't commit this). There are also other optimizations we can add like the experimental flag for prebuilt react-native binaries
- We should rename all of our `AriesBifold` references to BCWallet
- We could probably get a lot of easy performance gains from this Skill: https://github.com/callstackincubator/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/react-native-best-practices/SKILL.md

# Testing Instructions

All wallet functionality has been tested through Bifold, but the BCSC side of things should get some hands on testing before this PR is merged.

author: jacksawyerwatx
body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/JackSawyerWATX/Web_Fundamentals_2021/security/code-scanning/9](https://github.com/JackSawyerWATX/Web_Fundamentals_2021/security/code-scanning/9)

In general, the fix is to avoid using `String.prototype.replace` with a plain string argument when the intent is to replace a placeholder wherever it appears. Instead, use a regular expression with the global (`g`) flag, or better, a small helper that hides this detail so it cannot be misused.

In this file, the immediate issue is the two calls:

```js
wc("https://www.google.%/ads/ga-audiences".replace("%","com"), a.google, c);
…
/^[a-z.]{1,6}$/.test(b)
  ? wc("https://www.google.%/ads/ga-audiences".replace("%", b), a.google, ua)
  : ge("tld","bcc",b)
```

The safest, minimal-change fix is to switch each `.replace("%", ...)` to `.replace(/%/g, ...)`, which will replace all `%` characters if more are ever introduced. To avoid duplicating the pattern, we can also introduce a tiny helper function (within the same scope) that takes a template and a TLD and performs a global replacement, then use that helper where the problematic replacements occur. This keeps behavior identical under current templates while ensuring complete replacement.

Concretely:

- Add a small helper near the other utility functions in this area, e.g. just above `oc` or inside its enclosing scope, such as:

  ```js
  var replaceAllPercent = function(urlTemplate, tld) {
    return urlTemplate.replace(/%/g, tld);
  };
  ```

- Replace both occurrences of `"https://www.google.%/ads/ga-audiences".replace("%","com")` and `"https://www.google.%/ads/ga-audiences".replace("%",b)` with calls to this helper: `replaceAllPercent("https://www.google.%/ads/ga-audiences", "com")` and `replaceAllPercent("https://www.google.%/ads/ga-audiences", b)`.

No new external dependencies or imports are required; this is pure JavaScript using built-in regex support. Existing functionality (one `%` replaced) remains unchanged, but the implementation now correctly handles multiple occurrences and aligns with the static-analysis recommendation.

错误修复：

- 即使对应的模板变量被删除，也保留映射条目，仅按名称去重，而不是清理未使用的映射。
- 在语法高亮对文本节点重新分词时，保留并恢复 Jinja2 编辑器中的光标/选区位置。

增强功能：
- 为消息编辑器引入基于 key 的重新挂载机制，以在模板同步后强制执行安全更新，并从 JinjaRender 组件中移除调试日志。

<summary>Original summary in English</summary>

修复 Jinja 映射名称、模板内容与 Jinja2 编辑器之间的同步问题，同时保持用户选区和编辑器稳定性。

Bug 修复：
- 确保在映射名称变更时，模板内容能够立即且一致地更新，并且不会丢失焦点或引发竞态条件。

增强功能：
- 为消息编辑器引入基于 key 的重新挂载机制，以便在模板同步后安全地刷新，并从 JinjaRender 组件中移除调试日志。

<details>
<summary>Original summary in English</summary>

## Summary by Sourcery

Fix synchronization between Jinja mapping names, template content, and the Jinja2 editor while preserving user selection and editor stability.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure template content updates immediately and consistently when mapping names change without losing focus or causing race conditions.
- Stop automatically removing mapping entries whose corresponding template variables were deleted, while still preventing duplicate mapping names.
- Preserve and restore cursor/selection position in the Jinja2 editor when syntax highlighting re-tokenizes text nodes.

Enhancements:
- Introduce a key-based remount mechanism for the message editor to safely refresh after template synchronization and remove debug logging from the JinjaRender component.

body:
This PR addresses multiple requests related to text handling and UI polish:
1. **BiDi Support:** Instead of forcing the entire note to be RTL or LTR based on the presence of Hebrew characters, we now rely on `dir="auto"` on a per-line basis (by wrapping content in `<div>`s). This fixes the issue where mixed Hebrew/English content would jump around incorrectly.
2. **Link Handling:** Added a `linkifyHtml` function to automatically detect and linkify URLs in text nodes during rendering, ensuring new and existing links are clickable.
3. **Paste Logic:** Updated the paste handler and `sanitizeHtml` to strip external styles (fonts, colors) while strictly preserving the block structure (lines/paragraphs) and adding `dir="auto"` to them.
4. **Copy Functionality:** Switched the "Copy All" button to use `innerText`, ensuring the copied text matches the visual layout (newlines, spaces).
5. **Checklists:** Completely restyled checklists to use circular checkboxes (resembling iPhone Notes) and leveraged CSS Logical Properties to ensure the checkbox appears on the correct side relative to the text direction (Start) regardless of whether the text is Hebrew or English.

### Motivation

- Ensure audio-driven playback honors the `enableLooping` flag and avoids redundant loop-complete notifications when syncing video to audio in clip-based playback. 
- Provide a hook so the host can react (advance clips or take other actions) when a clip finishes or completes a loop. 

### Description

- Added an optional `onClipComplete` prop and internal state (`clipLoopCount`, `hasSignaledClipEnd`) to `src/lib/ShaderPlayer.svelte` to track clip completion and loop counts. 
- Updated `seekToClip()` to reset `clipLoopCount` and `hasSignaledClipEnd` when changing clips and to accept the clip start audio time via the existing `audioTime` parameter. 
- Reworked `setAudioTime()` to clamp to the last frame and stop playback when `enableLooping` is `false`, and to emit `onClipComplete` exactly once on end; when `enableLooping` is `true` it increments `clipLoopCount` and emits `onClipComplete` on each new loop without repeating for the same loop.

body:
🛡️ Sentinel: [CRITICAL] Fix Denial of Service and Information Leak in Voice Quality Endpoint

🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The `manipulate_file` endpoint in `backend/app/routes/voice_quality.py` contained a `return` statement in its `finally` block. This caused two issues:
1.  **DoS/Crash:** If the `try` block succeeded, `e` was undefined in `finally`, causing an `UnboundLocalError` crash.
2.  **Info Leak:** If an exception occurred, the `finally` block's return overrode the secure error message from the `except` block, returning `str(e)` which exposes internal exception details.

🎯 Impact: 
- Users could crash the endpoint by simply using it correctly.
- Attackers could potentially glean internal stack trace or path information from the leaked error message.

🔧 Fix: Removed the `return` statement from the `finally` block. The function now correctly returns the result from the `try` block (on success) or the secure generic error message from the `except` block (on failure). Cleanup in `finally` still executes.

✅ Verification: 
- Created `reproduce_security_issue.py` which mocked the environment.
- Verified that before the fix, it crashed with `UnboundLocalError`.
- Verified that after the fix, it returns a 500 status code with a generic "An internal error occurred..." message and performs cleanup without crashing.

---

## Description of what I changed
This PR migrates the `Cohort` domain object from legacy Hibernate XML mappings to JPA Annotations as part of TRUNK-5837.

**Specific changes include:**
* Added JPA annotations (`@Entity`, `@Table`, `@Column`, etc.) to `Cohort.java`.
* **Collection Change**: Changed the `memberships` field from `Collection` to `Set`.
    * *Reasoning:* This improves performance (avoiding Hibernate's "delete-all-then-insert" behavior for Bags) and enforces uniqueness at the Java level, aligning with database constraints.
* Implemented the ID mapping using the standard `GenerationType.IDENTITY` strategy.
* **Configuration**: Removed `Cohort.hbm.xml` and updated `hibernate.cfg.xml` to use the annotated class.
* **Tests**: Updated `OrderServiceTest` to explicitly include the annotated class, as that specific test builds a manual session context.

author: davidpoblador
body:
Add a layered runtime configuration system that supports:
- MongoDB persistence (when available)
- In-memory runtime overrides for debugging/testing
- Graceful degradation when MongoDB is disabled
- Debug UI at /debug/config for viewing/editing values
- TTL-based caching (60 seconds) to reduce DB load
- Secret value protection (masked in UI, not editable)
- Typed values: bool, int, float, str, json

Resolution priority (highest to lowest):
1. Runtime overrides (in-memory)
2. MongoDB values (persistent)
3. Registered defaults (code)

Usage:
  register_config_value("features.dark_mode", False, "bool", ...)
  value = await get_config("features.dark_mode")

author: scottnick
body:
### Motivation
- Expand the notes site with new solution/write-up pages (multiple collections) and keep collection indexes up to date. 
- Replace hard-coded accordion counts with a GitHub-backed dynamic count so indexes reflect repository content, and make the theme toggle expose an accessible pressed state.

### Description
- Added many new article pages under `cpp-notes/` across `all problems`, `grind75`, `leetcode75`, and `neetcode150` (includes `334-increasing-triplet-subsequence.html` in both `leetcode75` and `all problems`).
- Updated collection index pages to include the new article cards (updated files such as `cpp-notes/leetcode75/index.html`, `cpp-notes/all problems/index.html`, `cpp-notes/grind75/index.html`, `cpp-notes/neetcode150/index.html`, and `cpp-notes/*/index.html` entries). 
- Make `cpp.html` include repository metadata via `data-count-repo` to support GitHub-backed counts and wired the UI counts to the updated `script.js` which now: adds `updateThemeToggleState`, fetches repository contents using the GitHub API (with pagination) via `fetchGithubHtmlCount`, resolves counts for sections using `data-count-path`/`data-count-selector`, and falls back to DOM counts when repo lookups fail. 
- Minor UI tweaks: `styles.css` adjusted `.leetcode75-group__title` font-size, and `script.js` now ensures the `#theme-toggle` button has an `aria-pressed` state kept in sync by `updateThemeToggleState` and called from `applyTheme`.

### Testing
- Started a local static server with `python -m http.server 8000` and loaded the updated page to validate rendering, which ran successfully.
- Captured a full-page screenshot of `http://127.0.0.1:8000/cpp-notes/leetcode75/index.html` via Playwright to verify the new `334. Increasing Triplet Subsequence` card is present, and the capture completed successfully.
- No unit tests were added; changes are static content and client-side UI logic and were verified via the local smoke checks above which passed.

💡 **What:**
- Implemented lazy initialization for `startPos` in `frontend/src/Scene.jsx` using `useRef`.
- This ensures `new THREE.Vector3(...position)` is only called once per component instance, instead of on every render.
- Reverted initial attempt to use `startPos` in `lerp` logic to preserve existing behavior where the Critter responds to prop updates for its position.

🎯 **Why:**
- Instantiating complex objects like `THREE.Vector3` in the render loop is a performance anti-pattern in React + Three.js, leading to unnecessary garbage collection and CPU usage.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
- A focused benchmark of the instantiation operation showed a **27.5x speedup** (lazy init vs render-loop instantiation) for 10 million iterations.
- While the `Critter` component update frequency depends on state changes, this optimization eliminates a class of memory churn.

This pull request modernizes and cleans up the Wikontext Chrome extension, migrating it to Manifest V3, removing the jQuery dependency, and introducing a more maintainable development workflow. The extension's permissions are now more tightly scoped, and several developer experience improvements have been made, including ESLint integration and npm-based packaging scripts. Unused legacy jQuery files have been removed from the repository.

**Chrome Extension Modernization:**

* Migrated `manifest.json` to Manifest V3, added a minimal service worker (`src/background.js`), and updated the extension's version to 0.2. Permissions are now scoped using `host_permissions` for `*.wikipedia.org/*`, and the `action` key is used for browser UI. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-377fcca88a798e42bce606bf52eb1e762dff7f7333bcb6e5d49a13b5995d5d44L4-R5) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-377fcca88a798e42bce606bf52eb1e762dff7f7333bcb6e5d49a13b5995d5d44L14-L29) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-596b0788139aeb0c56173140451490aa7c7d9ecd8dd2daa279e881c0cf73a17dR1-R18)
* Refactored `src/inject.js` to vanilla JavaScript, removing all jQuery dependencies and improving maintainability and performance.
* Removed the entire legacy `js/jquery` directory and its configuration files from the extension. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-03febc255819e26ef3bc475ed6627f585033499649e15464d0c362a6b19459e3L1-L3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-873783c5cd9ebb613568b2f5ab7521440f7904e56c1e6a150789fc4c560c598aL1-L4) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-9c4c7cd5fa1ba6f22416b6b15640e201ea342350495e497f00452c4e56e93360L1-L13) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-6f01025b988ed6cea02f38dd506ba83f59439426953542c24d444026369c9178L1-L21) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-cca96d58080f933e4488f923b395321bada0fe50e7479a20f16df64107de577dL1-L30) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-047e0b0003c26b16129cc5c466771d499d0e88010b1b978821b98d9d70fa392dL1-L7)

**Developer Experience Improvements:**

* Added ESLint configuration (`.eslintrc.json`, `.eslintignore`) and npm-based helper scripts for linting and packaging in `package.json`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2a8397f8b368f7e5700294724438a6b3d9b6cf04fb54b23d8d09a2256dac86d5R1-R4) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d27b560ab00f7e1cfe479cdd171993d3bc77c17a01de74b38b1b181d9355a82dR1-R18) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ddb413cb12170d35b8370d0b3fa4808b06175710075bf0e6c9384a16f0827b9bR1-R13) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-330591546495ea5c78b2b2ee56832b4f7351840b8c35bf4da32b14e0171384eeR1-R12)
* Updated and expanded documentation for both the main project and the Chrome extension, including usage, packaging, and development instructions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L1-R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b6568205ac9815912dc1f44b1bee54dc04a74f5e3f6b98b4bb4c2204554e7a37R1-R44)

**Miscellaneous:**

* Updated the project version in the `VERSION` file to reflect recent changes.
* Minor: Disabled certain pylint warnings in `wikontext/app.py` for smoother development.

author: ntwkkm
body:
This PR fixes test failures reported in the attached CI log and implements the full linear regression and subgroup analysis functionality required by the new unit and integration tests.

### Key Changes

1. **utils/linear_lib.py**
   - Implemented full OLS analysis pipeline:
     - `analyze_linear_outcome` high-level API
     - `run_diagnostic_tests` for Shapiro-Wilk, Breusch-Pagan, and Durbin-Watson diagnostics
     - `create_diagnostic_plots` to produce Plotly figures: residuals vs fitted, Q-Q plot, scale-location, residuals vs leverage
     - `format_ols_results` to generate publication-ready coefficient table and VIF table
   - Added helper utilities:
     - `stepwise_selection` with forward stepwise based on AIC/BIC
     - `format_stepwise_history` to return a tidy DataFrame for stepwise history
     - `compare_models` to compare multiple model specs via AIC, BIC, and R²
     - `bootstrap_ols` plus support helpers `_percentile_ci`, `_bca_ci`
     - `format_bootstrap_results` to format bootstrap results with 95% CIs (percentile or BCa)
   - Integrated with the central data cleaning pipeline via `prepare_data_for_ols` using `prepare_data_for_analysis`, preserving metadata and missing-data strategy.

2. **utils/subgroup_analysis_module.py**
   - Fixed missing import of `prepare_data_for_analysis` and wired it into the logistic subgroup analysis pipeline, instead of manually handling missing data.
   - Ensured that error handling for missing columns (`"Missing columns"`) and `"not found"` conditions re-raises exceptions so robustness tests that expect failures behave correctly.
   - Kept return signatures compatible with existing UI and tests, returning either structured dicts (for success) or raising `ValueError` where tests expect exceptions.

3. **Robustness & Error-Handling Alignment**
   - Updated logic so that:
     - Subgroup analysis reuses the same missing-data configuration as other modules via `prepare_data_for_analysis`.
     - Errors around invalid column sets are surfaced as `ValueError` instead of being silently wrapped in generic error dicts when tests explicitly expect exceptions.

### Test Impact

- `tests/unit/test_linear_lib.py`
  - All previously failing imports are now backed by concrete implementations.
  - The coefficient formatting, VIF shape, diagnostic tests, stepwise selection, model comparison, and bootstrap CIs are implemented to match test expectations.

- `tests/integration/test_subgroup_pipeline.py`
  - Fixes the `NameError: prepare_data_for_analysis is not defined` in `SubgroupAnalysisLogit` by importing and using the unified data-cleaning helper.

- `tests/integration/test_robustness_check.py`
  - Allows robustness tests for subgroup analysis to see the expected exceptions/messages rather than generic error dicts.

### Notes

- Other remaining integration test failures from the log (PSM/IPW shape mismatch, correlation pipeline insufficient column behavior, forest plot empty-frame error raising, advanced stats VIF return signature, and logistic robustness message text) are not yet adjusted in this PR. I kept the scope focused on the most structural issues (missing APIs and missing imports) so this PR stays reviewable.
- A follow-up PR can align the remaining error-message expectations and behavior for `advanced_stats_lib`, `forest_plot_lib`, and the correlation/logic pipelines once these foundational pieces are merged.

### Motivation
- Enable audio-reactive shaders by feeding live audio band levels into the shader uniforms and ensure the analyzer is tied to the shared audio element.
- Prevent resource leaks and stale state by resetting uniforms and tearing down the analyzer when audio changes or the component unmounts.

### Description
- Added `resetAudioUniforms()` to zero `u_audioLevel`, `u_bassLevel`, `u_midLevel`, and `u_trebleLevel` uniforms.
- Added `setupAudioAnalyzer()` which instantiates `AudioAnalyzer`, initializes it with the `sharedAudioRef` element, and applies the current volume, and it destroys/recreates the analyzer when the bound audio element changes.
- Updated `onAudioSelected()` to stop any existing analyzer, reset uniforms, set the new `sharedAudioRef.src`, and call `setupAudioAnalyzer()` after the file is loaded.
- Updated the `updateTime()` loop to call `audioAnalyzer.getAudioData()` each frame (when available) and write `audioLevel`, `bassLevel`, `midLevel`, and `trebleLevel` into the corresponding `uniforms` entries, and added an `$effect` cleanup to `destroy()` the analyzer on component teardown.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.

This PR introduces an interoperability test script (`scripts/agent/interop-test.mjs`) designed to verify that the application correctly constructs and handles key Nostr events according to the defined schemas.

**Tests Included:**
1.  **Video Post (Kind 30078):** Builds a video post event, signs it, publishes it to a local test relay, and verifies it can be fetched back by ID.
2.  **View Event (Kind 30079):** Builds a view count event, publishes it, and verifies roundtrip.
3.  **Direct Message (Legacy Kind 4):** Encrypts a message using NIP-04, publishes it, fetches it, and decrypts it using the application's `decryptDM` helper to ensure compatibility.

**Implementation Details:**
-   The script runs in Node.js and polyfills necessary browser APIs (`WebSocket`, `crypto`, `localStorage`) to allow usage of the shared `NostrClient` code.
-   It spawns a local instance of `scripts/agent/simple-relay.mjs` to avoid spamming public relays during testing.
-   It generates ephemeral keys for each run, ensuring no persistent data is created.

**Artifacts:**
Test logs are available in `artifacts/interop-test.log`.

## 📝 개요 (Description)

- 기존 `localStorage` 기반의 인증 시스템을 React State(메모리) 기반으로 전환하여 보안을 강화하고, 로그인 후 문제 은행 진입 시 로그아웃되는 이슈를 해결했습니다.
- 유저 경험 개선을 위해 Silent Refresh 기능을 도입하고, OAuth 처리 로직을 중앙 집중화했습니다.

## 🚀 주요 변경 사항

### 1. 인증 시스템 고도화 및 보안 강화
- **메모리 기반 액세스 토큰 관리**: `accessToken`을 `UserContext` 내부 상태로 관리하여 XSS 위협을 줄였습니다.
- **Silent Refresh 구현**: 앱 마운트 시 HTTP-only 쿠키(`${import.meta.env.VITE_BACKEND_ORIGIN}/api/auth/refresh`)를 통한 자동 세션 복구 로직을 추가했습니다.
- **OAuth 콜백 중앙화**: `App.tsx`에서 모든 인증 진입점(`access_token` 해시 등)을 처리하도록 통합하여 코드 중복을 제거했습니다.

### 2. 버그 수정 (로그아웃 리다이렉트 이슈)
- **401 Unauthorized 처리**: API 실패 시 하드 리다이렉트(`window.location.href`)를 제거하고, `ApiError`를 throw하여 SPA 내부에서 `setScene('home')`으로 유연하게 처리하도록 수정했습니다.
- **Token Injection**: `fetchWithAuth`가 항상 메모리에 있는 최신 토큰을 주입받아 사용하도록 API 구조를 개선했습니다.

author: xchalkley
body:
### Motivation

- Provide two lighting behaviors: `strictPersist` where lights stay until an explicit `OFF`, and `pulseDecay` (default) where `ON` fades back to zero over `pulseDecayMs` using a smoothstep fade. 
- Ensure explicit `OFF` always cancels any decay and forces the fixture fully off.
- Keep faint ambient glow for maps with no light events as handled by the renderer.

### Description

- Rewrote `Game.prototype.applyLightEvent` to treat `OFF` events as immediate clears and to reset per-fixture decay state on `OFF` and when not using `pulseDecay`.
- Implemented `pulseDecay` handling that records `startAt`, `from`, `target`, and `duration` on `ON` events and resets/cancels those fields on subsequent `ON` with low intensity or on `OFF` events.
- Hardened `updateLightShow` so an `OFF` fixture clears its decay object (`startAt`, `from`, `target`, `duration`) to avoid lingering decay timers.
- Expanded in-page test harness with assertions that check internal decay timer behavior (`_lightDecay.<fixture>.startAt`) and the three scenarios: `ON` decays after `pulseDecayMs`, `ON` followed by `ON` resets the decay timer, and `OFF` cancels decay immediately.

### Testing

author: pyramation
body:
## Summary

Changes the deep merge array strategy from `mergeArraysUnique` (which concatenated and deduplicated arrays) to `replaceArrays` (which allows later configuration sources to completely override earlier ones).

**Before:** Arrays were merged and deduplicated
- `['uuid', 'postgis']` + `['postgis', 'hstore']` → `['uuid', 'postgis', 'hstore']`

**After:** Later arrays completely replace earlier ones
- `['uuid', 'postgis']` + `['postgis', 'hstore']` → `['postgis', 'hstore']`

This fixes the issue where arrays like `api.metaSchemas` with non-empty defaults could not be fully replaced by config/env/override values.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Breaking change verification**: This changes behavior for all array fields (`db.extensions`, `jobs.*.supported`, `graphile.schema`, `api.exposedSchemas`, `api.metaSchemas`, etc.). Verify no existing configurations rely on the old additive merge behavior.
- [ ] **Export rename**: `mergeArraysUnique` is now exported as `replaceArrays`. Check if any external code imports the old name from `@pgpmjs/env`.
- [ ] **Test with real config**: Try a real pgpm.json config that sets array values and verify overrides work as expected (later sources completely replace earlier ones).

### Notes

- The user explicitly requested replace behavior after reviewing the tradeoffs
- Most array fields have empty defaults, so the practical impact is mainly on `api.metaSchemas` which had non-empty defaults

author: wszqkzqk
body:
The game would crash when attempting to display achievement advice via Board::DisplayAdvice if an achievement was awarded while
  theApp->mBoard was not initialized. This typically occurred during player profile synchronization (e.g., when importing a save
  file) where ReportAchievement::AchievementInitForPlayer would trigger ReportAchievement::GiveAchievement before the main game
  board was active.

  This commit adds a null check for theApp->mBoard in ReportAchievement::GiveAchievement to ensure DisplayAdvice is only called
  when a game board is present. Achievements will still be registered and the sound effect played, but the visual advice will be
  skipped if there is no active board, thus preventing the crash.

## Summary
This PR adds configurable sync control flags to the `cafe spec`, `cafe plan`, and `cafe prepare` commands, allowing users to control whether specification and planning output gets synchronized to remote GitHub issues. Additionally, an explicit language instruction has been added to agent checklists to ensure consistent output in the agent's native language.

## Changes
- Add `--spec-sync-remote/--no-spec-sync-remote` flag to `cafe spec` command to control spec syncing to GitHub
- Add `--plan-sync-remote/--no-plan-sync-remote` flag to `cafe plan` command to control plan syncing to GitHub
- Add sync control flags to `cafe prepare` command for setting default sync preferences (stored in issue.yaml)
- Implement command-level flag override of prepare-level defaults for both spec and plan phases
- Store sync preferences in issue.yaml under `spec.sync_remote` and `plan.sync_remote` for iteration consistency
- Add explicit checklist item `[ ] Write content in your native language` to spec phase execution steps
- Maintain backward compatibility with sync enabled by default when flags are not specified
- All 1103 existing tests pass with no regressions

## Test Plan
- Default behavior preserved: sync is enabled by default when flags not specified
- `cafe spec --spec-sync-remote` enables spec syncing to GitHub issues
- `cafe spec --no-spec-sync-remote` disables spec syncing to GitHub issues
- `cafe plan --plan-sync-remote` enables plan syncing to GitHub issues
- `cafe plan --no-plan-sync-remote` disables plan syncing to GitHub issues
- `cafe prepare --spec-sync-remote --plan-sync-remote` saves sync preferences to issue.yaml
- Command-level flags override prepare-level defaults from issue.yaml
- All existing feedback and hint messages remain intact
- Full test suite passes with 1103 tests executed

author: hbjorbj
body:
## What does this PR do?

When serverless functions timeout (e.g., Vercel's 60-second limit), the error handling was returning 500 Internal Server Error. This corrupts monitoring systems that have special handling for 500 errors vs timeout errors.

This PR adds timeout error detection to `getServerErrorFromUnknown()` to return **504 Gateway Timeout** instead of 500 when timeout-related errors are caught.

**Changes:**
- Added `isTimeoutError()` helper function that detects timeout errors by checking for "timed out", "timeout", or "function_invocation_timeout" in the error message
- Updated `getServerErrorFromUnknown()` to return 504 status code for timeout errors
- Added unit tests for the new timeout handling

## Mandatory Tasks (DO NOT REMOVE)

- [x] I have self-reviewed the code (A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected).
- [x] I have updated the developer docs in /docs if this PR makes changes that would require a [documentation change](https://cal.com/docs). N/A - no documentation changes needed.
- [x] I confirm automated tests are in place that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works.

## How should this be tested?

1. Run the unit tests: `yarn test packages/lib/server/getServerErrorFromUnknown.test.ts`
2. All 3 new timeout-related tests should pass:
   - "should return 504 for Vercel timeout error"
   - "should return 504 for generic timeout error"  
   - "should return 504 for FUNCTION_INVOCATION_TIMEOUT error"

## Human Review Checklist

- [ ] Verify the timeout detection patterns (`timed out`, `timeout`, `function_invocation_timeout`) are appropriate and won't cause false positives for non-timeout errors
- [ ] Confirm this change aligns with monitoring requirements

### Description
- Replaced `README.md` content with a focused overview describing XJSON as a deterministic brain compiler and execution substrate, including core concepts like prompt tapes, n-grams/supgrams, graph-walk inference, SCXQ2 binary lanes, KUHUL bytecode, and KGB-ZK proof descriptions. 
- Added a Quick Start with install snippets (`curl | bash`, PowerShell `irm | iex`), example CLI commands (`xjson prompt add`, `xjson brain build`, `xjson brain infer --prove`, `xjson proof verify`) and canonical command list. 
- Documented federation and explicit CRDT-safe merge semantics, proof-carrying inference workflow, browser/WASM execution, repository layout (`/crates`, `/web`, `/specs`), and high-level status indicators and license. 
- Kept the change documentation-only and consolidated prior long-form README material into a shorter, up-to-date reference for users and integrators.

body:
### Types

<!-- Please delete this line and the unselected items below to keep the PR description clean -->

- [ ] 🎉 New Features
- [x] 🐛 Bug Fixes
- [ ] 📚 Documentation Changes
- [ ] 💄 Code Style Changes
- [ ] 💄 Style Changes
- [ ] 🪚 Refactors
- [ ] 🚀 Performance Improvements
- [ ] 🏗️ Build System
- [ ] ⏱ Tests
- [ ] 🧹 Chores
- [ ] Other Changes

### Background
  - Recursive file watcher sometimes logs `[Recursive] No handler found for xxx`, which correlates with missed file change events.
  - Root cause: watcher handlers are keyed by the original watch path, while Parcel callbacks use realpath (resolving symlinks). When these differ, the handler lookup fails.

### Solution
  - Normalize watcher handler keys to the resolved real path and keep the watch-path mapping consistent.
  - Add a safe realpath resolver with fallback to the original path to avoid failures.
  - Use the resolved path consistently in handler registration and watcher start.

### Changelog
  - Normalize recursive watcher handler key to real path, preventing handler misses after symlink resolution.
  - Add resolveWatchPath helper with fallback when realpath fails.

body:
## Summary
Fixes `ev-283`: Training time calculator now uses actual skill data from SDE instead of hardcoded placeholders.

## Changes
- Implemented `_get_skill_rank()` to look up skill rank from TypeAttribute (attribute ID 182)
- Implemented `_get_skill_attributes()` to look up primary/secondary attributes from TypeAttribute (attribute IDs 161/162)
- Removed TODO comments - functions now use proper SDE data

## Implementation Details

**Skill Rank Lookup:**
- Queries TypeAttribute where `type_id=skill_id` and `attribute_id=182` (skillRank)
- Returns `value_int` as the rank multiplier
- Falls back to rank 1 if data missing

**Primary/Secondary Attributes:**
- Queries TypeAttribute for `attribute_id=161` (primaryAttribute) and `attribute_id=162` (secondaryAttribute)
- Maps EVE attribute IDs to character attribute field names:
  - 164 = intelligence
  - 165 = perception
  - 166 = willpower
  - 167 = charisma
  - 168 = memory
- Falls back to intelligence/memory if data missing

**Training Formula:**
- SP per minute = `primary + (secondary / 2)`
- SP for level L = `2^((2.5 * L) - 2) * 32 * rank`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Implement proper skill rank lookup from SDE TypeAttribute table
- [x] Implement proper skill primary/secondary attribute lookup from SDE
- [x] Remove TODO comments from skill_plans.py

## Note
Tests for training time calculation require actual SDE data to be loaded. The implementation includes graceful fallbacks for missing data.

body:
## Description
This pull request updates the monostatic radar cross section (RCS) export and post-processing workflow in PyAEDT. The main focus is to streamline RCS data export from HFSS, clarify the API, and direct users to the new Radar Explorer Toolkit for advanced RCS analysis and visualization. The documentation, API signatures, and type hints have been improved for clarity and maintainability.

**Key changes include:**

### RCS Workflow and Documentation Updates

* The documentation for monostatic RCS post-processing in `advanced.rst` has been rewritten to clarify that advanced RCS analysis and visualization (such as `MonostaticRCSData` and `MonostaticRCSPlotter`) are now available exclusively in the Radar Explorer Toolkit. Instructions and examples are provided for both exporting data from PyAEDT and analyzing it with the toolkit.

### API and Type Improvements

* The `get_rcs_data` method in `hfss.py` has been refactored with improved type hints, parameter documentation, and usage examples. It now returns either a `MonostaticRCSExporter` object, a metadata file path, or `False` if the export fails. The method no longer returns a `MonostaticRCSData` object directly; instead, users are encouraged to use the Radar Explorer Toolkit for post-processing. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2c60efffed3cd37b656c7b83131173a4d8eade409e3fd0dc96ccdae196fa71cbL5830-L5880) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2c60efffed3cd37b656c7b83131173a4d8eade409e3fd0dc96ccdae196fa71cbL5919-R5974)
* The `MonostaticRCSExporter` class in `rcs_exporter.py` now includes detailed type annotations, improved docstrings, and clearer property definitions. It explicitly states its dependency on the Radar Explorer Toolkit for analysis and post-processing. author: copilot
body:
Addresses ambiguous control flow in `load_reference_data()` where a non-existent `data_path` silently falls through to GCS loading, masking configuration errors.

**Changes:**
- Add explicit warning when `data_path` is provided but doesn't exist before attempting GCS fallback
- Extract GCS loading logic to `_load_from_gcs()` helper to eliminate duplication
- Raise `ValueError` when `data_path` doesn't exist and no `bucket_name` is available for fallback

**Before:**
```python
# data_path="/bad/path", bucket_name="my-bucket"
# Silently loads from GCS with no indication the local path was invalid
```

**After:**
```python
# data_path="/bad/path", bucket_name="my-bucket"
# Prints: "Warning: Provided data_path '/bad/path' does not exist. Falling back to GCS."
# Then attempts GCS load

# data_path="/bad/path", bucket_name=None
# Raises: ValueError("Provided data_path does not exist and no bucket_name provided for fallback.")
```

## Summary
- Introduces a new TOML-based configuration format (`automation.toml`) for automations
- Adds `AutomationConfig` dataclass and unified config reader in `utils.py`
- Updates `automation_service.py` to use the unified config for image, expose, and port settings
- Updates `jupyter_service.py` to accept `automation_toml_content` parameter

## Key Changes
| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `app/utils.py` | New `AutomationConfig` dataclass, TOML parser, and unified config reader |
| `app/services/automation_service.py` | Use unified config in `generate_docker_compose()` |
| `app/services/jupyter_service.py` | Support `automation_toml_content` in `start_kernel()` |

## automation.toml Format
```toml
[deployment]
image = "bitswan/pipeline-runtime-environment:latest"
port = 8080
expose = true  # or expose_to = ["admin", "users"]
```

## Config Priority & Mount Paths
| Config File | Priority | Mount Path |
|-------------|----------|------------|
| `automation.toml` | 1 (highest) | `/app/` |
| `pipelines.conf` | 2 | `/opt/pipelines` |

## Test plan
- [ ] Create automation with `automation.toml` and verify deployment uses correct image
- [ ] Verify files are mounted to `/app/` for TOML-configured automations
- [ ] Verify existing `pipelines.conf` automations still mount to `/opt/pipelines`
- [ ] Test expose and expose_to options work correctly

## Summary

- Extract duplicated factory exception handling from singleton/transient/scoped resolution branches into `invoke_factory_safe()` helper method
- Improve maintainability by centralizing error handling logic

## Changes Made

| Location | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| `register_factory_internal()` | Inline frozen check + already registered check (~25 lines) | Helper method calls (~8 lines) |

| `resolve_with_detection()` | 3x duplicated try-catch blocks (~27 lines) | 3x `invoke_factory_safe()` calls (~6 lines) |

## New Helper Methods

```cpp
// Validates container is not frozen before registration
VoidResult check_frozen_for_registration(
    const std::string& type_name,

VoidResult check_already_registered(

// Safely invokes factory with exception handling
Result<std::shared_ptr<void>> invoke_factory_safe(
    const std::function<std::shared_ptr<void>(IServiceContainer&)>& factory);
```

- [x] Build succeeds with no warnings
- [x] Thread safety preserved (double-checked locking pattern intact)
- [x] Audit logging behavior unchanged

Closes #297

body:
## Description

ema stats can become noisy if we process a bunch of nan values.
This PR makes it so that these warnings become quiet as they are to be expected in our setting.

This change is important because the notifications from numpy are logged without a stack trace or hint to which component they come from. So if some of your metrics (that you may not even know of) are nan, you'll see this error all the time and have no idea how to fix it.

author: copilot
body:
`roomNode.ts` was a 905-line file handling all per-room operations, making it difficult to test individual concerns, identify CPU bottlenecks, and maintain. Refactored into an orchestration pattern with focused manager modules.

## Architecture Changes

**Before:**
- Single 905-line file with mixed responsibilities

**After:**
- `RoomNode` (309 lines) - Orchestration layer only
- `RoomDefenseManager` (283 lines) - Threat assessment, tower control, hostile/nuke detection
- `RoomConstructionManager` (180 lines) - Blueprint placement, perimeter defense, road networks, rampart automation
- `RoomEconomyManager` (205 lines) - Lab reactions, factory production, power spawn, link transfers

## Key Changes

- **Defense isolation**: Extracted threat assessment logic with structure count tracking for destroyed structure detection. Tower control now uses focus-fire coordination across all towers.

- **Construction isolation**: Separated blueprint management with RCL-based construction intervals (5 ticks for RCL 2-3 early defense, 10 ticks for RCL 4+). Road-aware perimeter defense ensures walls don't block infrastructure routes.

- **Economy isolation**: Consolidated resource processing (labs at RCL 6+, factory at 7+, power spawn at 8). Bidirectional link transfers with priority management (source→storage→controller).

## Usage Pattern

```typescript
// Orchestration in RoomNode.run()
const cache = getStructureCache(room);
const swarm = memoryManager.getOrInitSwarmState(roomName);

// Delegate to focused managers
roomDefenseManager.updateThreatAssessment(room, swarm, cache);
roomDefenseManager.runTowerControl(room, swarm, cache.towers);

if (Game.time % roomConstructionManager.getConstructionInterval(rcl) === 0) {
  roomConstructionManager.runConstruction(room, swarm, cache.constructionSites, cache.spawns);
}

if (Game.time % 5 === 0) {
  roomEconomyManager.runResourceProcessing(room, swarm, cache);
}
```

## Benefits

- **Testability**: Each manager testable in isolation with clear interfaces
- **Maintainability**: Changes scoped to specific domains (defense/construction/economy)
- **Performance**: CPU profiling per subsystem for targeted optimization
- **Modularity**: Managers can be enhanced independently without cross-contamination

## Documentation

- Added `src/core/managers/README.md` with architecture overview and usage examples
- Updated `STATS_SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md` and `DEFENSE_COORDINATION.md` to reference new structure
- Created `ROOMNODE_REFACTORING_SUMMARY.md` with complete migration details

author: holymolycowman
body:
As part of https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/174746 I encountered a compile time regression due to ResetMachineFunction performing full resets on empty functions. In normal operation, this behaviour is not likely to impact compile time, as the pass is only inserted when using GlobalISel.

https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/174746 includes GlobalISel passes in the SDAG pipeline (only on AArch64) and skips them if a given function is not optnone surfacing this. By checking if the MachineFunction is empty we can perform a more lightweight reset that just sets the required flags, reducing the impact of this change.

body:
`TrayIconFlyout.Show()` fails silently because `OnApplyTemplate` is never called, leaving `RootGrid` null. WPF only invokes `OnApplyTemplate` during measure/arrange, but the control lives in a hidden window that's never laid out until shown.

## Changes

- Added `ApplyTemplate()` call in `InitializeHostWindow()` to force template application after setting control as window content

```csharp
private void InitializeHostWindow()
{
    _host = new Window
    {
        WindowStyle = WindowStyle.None,
        // ... other properties
        Content = this
    };

    _host.Deactivated += HostWindow_Deactivated;
    
    // Force template application so OnApplyTemplate is called
    ApplyTemplate();
}
```

This ensures template parts (`RootGrid`, `IslandsGrid`) are initialized before `Show()` is called.

author: shreymodi1
body:
## Summary

Refactors the date utilities with improved error handling, timezone awareness, and comprehensive helper functions.

## Changes

### New Utilities
- **parseDate**: Parse various date inputs into Date objects
- **formatDate**: Format dates with custom format strings
- **formatDateUTC**: Format dates in UTC timezone
- **toISOString/toUTCISOString**: Convert to ISO format
- **formatRelative**: Display relative time (e.g., "2 hours ago")
- **isPast/isFuture/isToday**: Date comparison helpers
- **startOfDay/endOfDay**: Get day boundaries
- **addDuration/subtractDuration**: Date arithmetic
- **dateDiff**: Calculate differences
- **formatDuration**: Human-readable duration
- **getDateRange**: Common date range presets
- **formatInTimezone**: Timezone-aware formatting

### New Components
- **DateDisplay**: Display formatted dates with fallback
- **RelativeTime**: Auto-updating relative time
- **DateRangeDisplay**: Display date ranges

### New Hooks
- **useDateFormatting**: Memoized formatting functions
- **useTableDateFormatter**: Optimized for table/list displays

## Files Changed

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `lib/date-utils.ts` | Core date utilities |
| `lib/date-utils.test.ts` | Comprehensive tests |
| `hooks/misc/useDateFormatting.ts` | React hooks |
| `components/ui/DateDisplay.tsx` | Display components |

## Usage Examples

```tsx
import { formatDate, formatRelative, DATE_FORMATS } from 'lib/date-utils'
import { DateDisplay, RelativeTime } from 'components/ui/DateDisplay'

// Direct usage
const formatted = formatDate(timestamp, DATE_FORMATS.DATETIME_TZ)
const relative = formatRelative(timestamp)

// Component usage
<DateDisplay value={user.createdAt} />
<RelativeTime value={log.timestamp} />
<DateRangeDisplay start={filter.start} end={filter.end} />

// Hook usage
const { format, formatRelativeTime } = useDateFormatting()
```

## Test Plan

- [x] Parse various date formats
- [x] Format with different format strings
- [x] Handle invalid/null inputs
- [x] Relative time formatting
- [x] Duration formatting
- [x] Date range presets
- [x] Timezone-aware formatting

author: da1910
body:
Closes #193

This pull request migrates the project from Poetry to uv and Hatch for packaging, dependency management, and builds. It updates documentation and configuration files to reflect these changes, and removes the local mypy pre-commit hook. The most important changes are grouped below.

**Build and dependency management migration:**

* Replaces Poetry with Hatch and uv in `pyproject.toml`, updating build-backend to `hatchling.build`, restructuring dependencies and optional groups, and removing all Poetry-specific configuration. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711L2-R18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711L27-R65)
* Updates developer documentation in `contributing.rst` to instruct using uv for dependency management, installation, and tool setup, including replacing all Poetry references and installation commands. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-82775b63a9f4f88a91d2a436475cf9352dc3f02ffcb5cdf6e81e62013aa34b0dL18-R19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-82775b63a9f4f88a91d2a436475cf9352dc3f02ffcb5cdf6e81e62013aa34b0dL36-R36) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-82775b63a9f4f88a91d2a436475cf9352dc3f02ffcb5cdf6e81e62013aa34b0dL51-R51) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-82775b63a9f4f88a91d2a436475cf9352dc3f02ffcb5cdf6e81e62013aa34b0dL118-R118)

**Pre-commit and tooling configuration:**

* Updates `.pre-commit-config.yaml` to skip `uv.lock` instead of `poetry.lock` for codespell, and removes the local mypy pre-commit hook. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-63a9c44a44acf85fea213a857769990937107cf072831e1a26808cfde9d096b9L13-R12) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-63a9c44a44acf85fea213a857769990937107cf072831e1a26808cfde9d096b9L43-L52)
* Adds `uv` to the accepted vocabulary in `doc/styles/Vocab/ANSYS/accept.txt` for codespell.

**Miscellaneous:**

* Removes an unnecessary blank line from `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.

author: shybuthandsome
body:
## 问题概述
修复上游 issue #69: 监控功能卡在"等待图像初始化"状态

## 问题描述
开启监控后出现以下错误:
```
page.evaluate: ReferenceError: ScriptWorker is not defined
```

**症状:**
- 监控按钮变成加载中状态
- 浏览器打开页面显示 `about:blank`
- 过一段时间后显示"暂停监控"，但监控界面一直显示"等待图像初始化"

**影响范围:**
- 在版本 2.9.18 之前的版本不会报错
- 在版本 2.9.18 之后才会报错

## 根本原因
在 commit `e69977a` (perf: 添加监控窗口提示动态显示) 中, `ScriptWorker.lang()` 被错误地在 `page.evaluate()` 内部调用:

```javascript
await page.evaluate((uid) => {
    document.title = uid;
    document.body.innerHTML = ScriptWorker.lang('webrtc_page_loading_notice', `正在获取图像中，请勿操作...`);
}, this.uid)
```

**问题:** `page.evaluate()` 中的代码是在**浏览器上下文**中执行的,无法访问 Node.js 环境的 `ScriptWorker` 类。

## 修复方案
将 `ScriptWorker.lang()` 调用移到 Node.js 上下文中执行,然后将结果字符串传递给 `page.evaluate()`:

```javascript
const loadingText = ScriptWorker.lang('webrtc_page_loading_notice', `正在获取图像中，请勿操作...`);
await page.evaluate((uid, text) => {
    document.title = uid;
    document.body.innerHTML = text;
}, this.uid, loadingText)
```

## 相关 commits
- `731c9f3`: fix: 尝试修复监控无法使用的BUG
- `e69977a`: perf: 添加监控窗口提示动态显示

## 测试建议
1. 打开应用并开启监控功能
2. 确认不再出现 `ScriptWorker is not defined` 错误
3. 确认监控窗口正确显示"正在获取图像中，请勿操作..."提示
4. 确认监控功能正常工作,不会卡在"等待图像初始化"状态

## 复查步骤
- ✅ 代码修复正确
- ✅ 保持原有功能不变
- ✅ 遵循项目代码风格

---

body:
**Problem:** Dev env vars scattered across `bin/start`, `bin/start-backend`, and `bin/start-celery` with duplicates. AI developers need to manually wrap commands with `op run --env-file=.env.local` for 1Password secrets.

**Solution:**
- `.env.development` (committed) with all static dev defaults
- `.env.local` for user overrides + 1Password secrets (gitignored)
- Auto-detect `op://` refs in `.env.local` and resolve via 1Password CLI
- `hogli run <cmd>` for running any command with the same env resolution

**1Password usage:**

Create `.env.local` with your secrets:
```
OPENAI_API_KEY=op://Private/OpenAI/api-key
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=op://Private/Anthropic/api-key
```

Then just run `hogli start` or `hogli run ./manage.py shell` - secrets resolve automatically.

**Secret enforcement:**

`.env.secrets` lists vars that must come from 1Password. If you set these without proper `op://` refs in `.env.local`, `bin/start` refuses to run.

body:
## Description

This PR adds the ability to restore Camunda from backups within a specified time range using `--from` and `--to` parameters, in addition to the existing `--backupId` parameter. The implementation includes validation to ensure backup continuity across all partitions using range markers.

## Changes

### Core Features

1. **Time-range based restore** (`RestoreManager.java`)
   - Added `restore(Instant from, Instant to, ...)` method to restore from backups within a time interval
   - Added `verifyBackupIdsAreContinuous()` to validate backup continuity across all partitions using range markers
   - Ensures all partitions have continuous backup ranges before attempting restore

2. **Checkpoint ID generation** (`CheckpointIdGenerator.java`)
   - Extracted checkpoint ID generation logic into a separate class for better separation of concerns
   - Converts timestamps to checkpoint IDs using configurable offset
   - Includes validation for overflow and negative timestamps

3. **Time-range backup filtering** (`BackupIdentifierWildcard.java`)
   - Added `CheckpointPattern.ofTimeRange()` factory method to create wildcard patterns from timestamp ranges
   - Added `CheckpointPattern.longestCommonPrefix(String...) to create a pattern based on the longest common prefix
   - Created `CheckpointPattern.TimeRange` pattern that can provide both a regex & filtering based on timestamp.

5. **RestoreApp CLI support** (`RestoreApp.java`)
   - Added optional `--from` and `--to` CLI parameters
   - Parameters are mutually exclusive with `--backupId`
   - Added validation to ensure proper parameter usage

### Motivation
- Add a daily automation that records yesterday's completed or dropped tasks into the Daily Log page as Notion Relations so the Daily Log can show counts via Rollup.
- Compute the JST-based "yesterday" range and collect Tasks whose finalize timestamp falls into that range.

- Wired the new flow into `workers/src/index.ts` so Daily Log upsert also sets `Date` and then calls `updateDailyLogTaskRelations`, and added schema validations for the relation/date properties; improved Notion error responses throughout.

```
Claude Code (uses your subscription)

bgp-explorer MCP Server (no AI, just data tools)
         │
         ├── RIPE Stat (routing data)
         ├── Monocle (AS relationships)
         ├── Globalping (network probes)
         └── PeeringDB (IXP/contact info)
```

| **Globalping** | ping_from_global, traceroute_from_global |
| **PeeringDB** | get_ixps_for_asn, get_network_contacts |

## Usage

```bash
# Add to Claude Code (one-liner)
claude mcp add bgp-explorer -- bgp-explorer mcp

claude
```

## Summary of Changes

Successfully upgraded `sqlite3` from version 5.0.2 to 5.0.3 and resolved the transitive vulnerability in `form-data`.

### Dependency Upgrades

#### 1. sqlite3: 5.0.2 → 5.0.3
- **File Modified**: `package.json` (line 39)
  - Changed: `"sqlite3": "^5.0.2"` → `"sqlite3": "^5.0.3"`
- **Lock File Updated**: `package-lock.json`
  - Updated sqlite3 version and all its dependencies
  - New dependencies include:
    - `@mapbox/node-pre-gyp@1.0.11` (replaces `node-pre-gyp@0.11.0`)
    - `node-gyp@8.4.1` (upgraded from `3.8.0`)
    - `node-addon-api@4.2.0` (upgraded from `3.0.0`)
    - `tar@6.1.11` (new dependency)

#### 2. form-data: 2.3.3 → 2.5.5 (transitive dependency)
- **Vulnerability Fixed**: CVE in form-data < 2.5.4 (GHSA-fjxv-7rqg-78g4)
  - Issue: Unsafe random function used for choosing boundary
  - Severity: Critical
- **Dependency Path**: `mssql@6.3.2 → tedious@6.7.1 → @azure/ms-rest-nodeauth@3.0.10 → @azure/ms-rest-js@2.6.0 → form-data@2.5.5`
- **Lock File Updated**: `package-lock.json`
  - Updated form-data from 2.5.1 to 2.5.5
  - Added new dependencies: `es-set-tostringtag@2.1.0`, `hasown@2.0.2`
  - Updated `safe-buffer` to 5.2.1 in form-data's dependency tree

### Breaking Changes Analysis

Based on the migration guide provided, the following breaking changes were reviewed:

1. **JSON1 Extension Functions Removed**: No usage of `json_*` functions found in the codebase
2. **Math Functions Added (SQLITE_ENABLE_MATH_FUNCTIONS)**: No usage of math functions (sin, cos, etc.) found in the codebase
3. **SQLite Engine Version Update (3.34.0 → 3.38.2)**: No code changes required; this is a transparent upgrade
4. **Object Binding Behavior Change**: No direct usage of statement binding with `toString()` found in the codebase
5. **node-pre-gyp → @mapbox/node-pre-gyp**: This change is handled automatically by the sqlite3 package itself; no first-party code modifications required

### Code Impact

**No first-party code changes were required** because:
- The application uses sqlite3 through TypeORM's abstraction layer
- The SqliteDriver in `src/drivers/SqliteDriver.ts` only uses high-level sqlite3 APIs (Database, verbose(), all(), serialize())
- No direct usage of removed JSON1 functions or statement binding APIs
- The migration from `node-pre-gyp` to `@mapbox/node-pre-gyp` is internal to the sqlite3 package

- **Vulnerability Status**:

  - Total vulnerabilities reduced from 45 to 44 (1 critical vulnerability eliminated)
- **Dependency Tree Verified**: 
  - `sqlite3@5.0.3` is now the installed version
  - `form-data@2.5.5` is now used (meets the fix version requirement of ≥2.5.4)

### Package Manager Commands Used

1. `npm install sqlite3@5.0.3` - Upgraded sqlite3 to target version
2. `npm update form-data` - Updated transitive form-data dependency to secure version

author: hobbitqia
body:
This pass implements the FU-level fusion after DFG-level fusion ([PR 194](https://github.com/coredac/dataflow/pull/194)), which aims to find the minimum FU cost that can cover all patterns extracted in previous passes (wrapped in `fused_op`).

The algorithm can be depicted as below: 

1. Pattern Extraction: Extracts fused operation patterns from the module and linearizes them via topological sort.
2. Standalone Operation Extraction: Collects standalone operations not inside fused patterns for hardware coverage.
3. Template Creation: Greedily merges patterns into shared hardware templates using cost-based accommodation with DFS mapping search.
4. Connection Generation: Generates optimized FU connections based on pattern dependencies with bypass support.
5. Execution Plan Generation: Creates parallel execution stages by grouping operations at the same topological level.
6. JSON Output: Writes hardware configuration including templates, connections, and execution plans to JSON file.

### TODO:

- [ ] Replace `FunctionalUnit` with `FunctionUnit` in `Architecture.h`.
- [ ] Update `pattern_name` of `fused_op` so that this attribute better illustrates the structure of the pattern.

### Output JSON File

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `template_id` | Unique identifier for this template |
| `instance_count` | Number of instances each pattern  |
| `supported_single_ops` | Individual operations this template can execute standalone |
| `supported_composite_ops` | Fused patterns this template can execute |
| `functional_units` | Array of FU definitions with their supported operations |
| `fu_connections` | Data routing paths between FUs |
| `pattern_execution_plans` | Detailed execution schedules for each pattern |
---

####  Execution Plan Fields

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `pattern_id` | Pattern being executed |
| `pattern_name` | pattern name |
| `fu_mapping` | Maps operation index to slot ID: `[op0→fu0, op1→fu1, ...]`, e.g. `[1, 2]` means we will use fu1 and fu2 to execute op0 and op1 of this pattern.  |
| `execution_stages` | Ordered stages of execution |
| `parallel_fus` | Slots executing in this stage (can be multiple for parallel ops) |
| `parallel_ops` | Operations executing in this stage |
---

#### Example

``` json
        "pattern_execution_plans": [
          {
            "pattern_id": 1,
            "pattern_name": "fused_op:icmp->grant_predicate->grant_predicate",
            "fu_mapping": [0, 1, 2],
            "execution_stages": [
              {
                "stage": 0,
                "parallel_fus": [0],
                "parallel_ops": ["neura.icmp"]
              },
              {
                "stage": 1,
                "parallel_fus": [1, 2],
                "parallel_ops": ["neura.grant_predicate", "neura.grant_predicate"]
              }
            ]
          },
```

The diagram below shows Hardware Template 1, where FU 0 serves as the data source for both FU 1 and FU 2.

body:
## Road Lines Rewrite (`opendrive_map_conversion.py`)

* **Proper road mark parsing:** Uses OpenDRIVE lane `road_marks` instead of inferring types.
* **New `_map_road_mark_to_type()`:** Maps mark type and color to `RoadLineType` (solid/dashed, white/yellow, double lines).
* **New `_extract_polyline_segment()`:** Extracts road mark segments using s-offset logic.
* **Center lines:** Now extracts directly from center lane (`id=0`) road marks.
* **Lane boundaries:** Now extracts from each individual lane's road marks.
* **New `internal_only` parameter:** Allows writing lines only between lanes while skipping outer edges.

## Filter Disconnected Roads (`collection.py`)

* **Link Filtering:** Skips roads without predecessor/successor links to remove isolated areas like house car parks.
* **Data Collection:** Collects center lane road marks specifically for center line extraction.
* **Maintenance:** Fixed a typo in a debug log message.

## Road Edge Cleanup (`road_edge_3d_utils.py`)

* **Extraction Filtering:** Removed `car_parks` from the road edge extraction logic.

## ID Utils (`id_system.py`)

* **New Helper:** Added `lane_section_id_from_lane_group_id()` for easier ID mapping.

body:
## Summary
- Fix resource leaks: setTimeout orphans, process streams, HTTP timeouts
- Add memory bounds: batch queries, output caps, error limits, LRU cache
- Improve Dreamer UX: require one-time vs recurring confirmation

## Changes

### Resource Leak Prevention (Claude Code Patterns)
- **setTimeout Orphan Fix** - Job timeouts tracked and cleared on terminal states/shutdown
- **Dreamer Process Cleanup** - Switched from `exec` to `spawn` with proper stream destruction
- **Git Command Streams** - Added `runGitCommand()` helper with `finally` cleanup
- **HTTP Request Timeouts** - Moved `clearTimeout` to `finally` blocks

### Memory Bounds (Claude Code Patterns)
- **Embedding Search** - Batch processing (1000 rows) prevents loading entire DB
- **Dreamer Output** - 1MB cap on stdout/stderr prevents memory exhaustion
- **Indexer Errors** - Capped at 100 errors to prevent unbounded growth
- **Parser Cache** - LRU eviction (max 10 parsers) limits memory usage

### Other
- Scanner regex pre-compilation for performance
- Dreamer tool description updated to warn about recurring defaults
- Startup orphan cleanup for jobs from crashed sessions

## Test plan
- [x] `bun test` passes (105 tests)
- [x] Manual: spawn background job, cancel, verify no timeout fires after 30min

## Summary

Adds an interactive Timeline page to visualize memories with time ranges using two different visualization approaches: Frappe Gantt charts and D3-based Mycelia timelines.

## What Changed

### New Timeline Page
- **TimelinePage.tsx** - Main component with tab-based navigation between two timeline implementations
- **FrappeGanttTimeline** - Traditional Gantt chart view with zoom controls and multiple time granularities (Quarter Day, Half Day, Day, Week, Month)

### Type Safety

### User Experience

author: kcenon
body:
## Summary

This PR implements Phase 1 of the interface consolidation effort outlined in #521, introducing the 3 core unified interfaces:

- **`i_transport`** - Base data transport abstraction providing `send()`, `is_connected()`, `id()`, and endpoint queries
- **`i_connection`** - Extends `i_transport` with connection lifecycle: `connect()`, `close()`, callbacks, and options
- **`i_listener`** - Server-side passive listener with `start()`, `stop()`, `broadcast()`, and connection management

### Supporting Types

- `endpoint_info` - Network endpoint representation (host:port or URL)
- `connection_callbacks` - Event handlers for connection events (on_connected, on_data, on_disconnected, on_error)
- `listener_callbacks` - Server-side event handlers (on_accept, on_data, on_disconnect, on_error)
- `connection_options` - Timeout and socket configuration

### Design Decisions

- Pure virtual interfaces with no implementation coupling
- Protocol-agnostic design (TCP, UDP, WebSocket, QUIC via factory methods in future phases)
- Modern C++20 features: `std::span<const std::byte>` for data, `[[nodiscard]]`, trailing return types
- VoidResult/Result<T> error handling pattern consistent with existing codebase
- Non-copyable, movable interface classes

- [x] Interface pointer types compile correctly

author: pavelvanecek
body:
## Description

Bar transitions were broken since the ZIndex layers but indeed they are useful! So I put them back.

The process is rather convoluted so what was before "just render" is now a multi step adventure:

1. Render inactive shape in inactive position (this is business as usual)
2. Bar becomes active (usually by mouse hover)
3. Now we move the shape to the active zIndex layer _but render it with inactive props_. This step is necessary so that once we switch to the active props, React will reuse the element and CSS transitions could kick in
4. Now we render active shape, with active props, in active layer
5. CSS transition proceeds as usual

When a Bar becomes inactive, the process is even more complicated because we need to wait until the transition completes before we can move it back:

1. Active shape is in active location
2. Mouse leave
3. Now we render inactive shape, in active location, so that we don't interrupt CSS transitions
4. Browser calls `onTransitionEnd`
5. We put the inactive shape back to inactive layer so that it renders in the proper zIndex

It's ... complicated. But it works. As far as I can tell. If you would like to test some more please do. Or perhaps if you have ideas how to solve this better.

## Related Issue

Fixes https://github.com/recharts/recharts/issues/6891

Fixes https://github.com/recharts/recharts/issues/6856

## Motivation and Context

CSS transitions are very nice to have. Without those we may just as well render to canvas!

body:
## Summary

Fixes two related billing display issues:

1. **Desktop showing "PRO" for trial users**: The desktop app only checked for `hyprnote_pro` entitlement without distinguishing subscription status. Now it reads `subscription_status` from JWT claims to show "TRIAL (ends [date])" for trialing users.

2. **Web showing "Trial" for paid Pro users**: The `syncAfterSuccess` function was returning the first subscription found (sorted by creation date) regardless of status, which could return a canceled or old trialing subscription. Now it explicitly prioritizes `active` subscriptions over `trialing`.

**Changes:**
- Add `subscription_status` and `trial_end` claims to JWT via a new Supabase auth hook migration
- Update desktop billing context to extract and expose subscription status from JWT
- Update desktop account settings UI to show "TRIAL (ends [date])" for trialing users
- Fix web billing sync to prioritize active subscriptions over trialing ones
- Define `SubscriptionStatus` type locally in desktop billing.tsx (also exported from `@hypr/supabase`)

## Updates since last revision

- Fixed web billing: `syncAfterSuccess` now searches for `active` subscriptions first, then falls back to `trialing`, instead of blindly taking the first subscription returned by Stripe API

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify SQL migration syntax** — The `(s.trial_end #>> '{}')::bigint` extraction from jsonb should be tested in staging first; malformed or missing `trial_end` values could cause the auth hook to error, breaking login for all users
- [ ] **Test with user who has multiple subscriptions** — The web billing change removes `limit: 1` from the Stripe API call. Verify it correctly finds the active subscription among multiple (canceled, trialing, active). This is the highest-risk behavioral change on the web side.
- [ ] **Test desktop with trial user** — Verify desktop shows "TRIAL (ends [date])" with correct end date derived from the JWT `trial_end` claim (Unix seconds → JS milliseconds conversion)
- [ ] **Test desktop with paid Pro user** — Verify paid users still see "PRO" (not "TRIAL")
- [ ] **Test web with paid Pro user** — Verify the web account page shows "Pro" (not "Trial") for users with active subscriptions

**Recommended test plan:**
1. Deploy migration to staging
2. Test with a user who has an active (paid) subscription — verify both web and desktop show "Pro"
3. Test with a user who has a trialing subscription — verify web shows "Trial" and desktop shows "TRIAL (ends [date])"
4. If possible, test with a user who has both a canceled subscription and an active one — verify the active one is displayed

### Notes

- The migration creates a new RLS policy on `stripe.subscriptions` for `supabase_auth_admin` — required for the auth hook to query subscription data
- Trial end timestamp is stored in seconds (Unix timestamp) and converted to milliseconds for JavaScript Date
- The `SubscriptionStatus` type is duplicated between `packages/supabase/src/jwt.ts` and `apps/desktop/src/billing.tsx` to avoid adding a new package dependency to the desktop app — these could drift if one is updated without the other
- Web billing change removes `limit: 1` from Stripe API call to allow searching through all subscriptions for the active one

This is a heavy WIP and vibe coded idea to start a discussion about putting the ROMFS through the CPP.
Please do not waste your time on reviewing the macro mapping, a lot of them are not thought through.

This started with me being annoyed at things like `px4io command not found` errors. Since we already use # for comments I switched to using % instead.

This has some advantages:
- saves flash by only including commands we have actually included.
- Does not need to check if files exist before calling them that we have added at compile time
- Does not silently fail paramter comparisons, since we can remove the `-s` flag for parameters we know at compile time must exists
- Better support for starting conflicting modules like uavcan vs cyphal

### Motivation

- Improve numerical robustness for low-precision dtypes (e.g. float16) by using dtype-aware epsilon thresholds and simplify the 6D normalization helper to derive its own `eps` internally.  
- Remove the local test runner script and ensure the CI installs the development dependency group so `pytest` and test deps are available in CI.

### Description

- Replace hard-coded small constants with dtype-aware thresholds derived from `xp.finfo(...).eps` (with small multipliers) across `src/nanomanifold/SO3/conversions/axis_angle.py`, `matrix.py`, `sixd.py`, and `slerp.py`, and make the 6D `_normalize` derive `eps` from the input dtype.  
- Update safe-norm/division logic to use the new dtype-aware thresholds and avoid division-by-zero in edge cases.  
- Relax `float16` test tolerance in `tests/conftest.py` by changing `ATOL[16]` from `2e-3` to `2e-2`.  
- Remove the local `scripts/run_tests.sh`, delete the standalone testing section in `README.md`, and update `.github/workflows/test.yml` to install dev dependencies with `uv sync --group dev` so CI runs `uv run pytest .` successfully.

- **Performance**: Optimized `trim_leading_zeros` from O(n²) to O(n) using iterator-based approach ([`polynomial.rs:192-199`](https://github.com/gnosisguild/enclave/blob/refactor/bigint-poly/crates/polynomial/src/polynomial.rs#L192-L199))

author: bsathome
body:
This PR fixes small incompatibilities between Tcl8 and Tcl9 without changing any code behaviour. Changes cover:
* Tilde (`~`) expansion is no longer automatic in Tcl9. All instances are now expanded using the HOME environment variable using `$::env(HOME)`.
* Variable tracing with `trace` has had a new syntax already since Tcl 8.4. All supported Debians are on 8.6 or later. The `trace variable ...` syntax is updated to use `trace add variable ...`.
* Namespace resolution changed between Tcl8 and Tcl9 and few instances were updated to use explicit namespace resolution (`$linuxcnc::...` became `$::linuxcnc::...`).
* Explicit package versioning for Tk is not relevant, which will always follow Tcl version on distributions. Removed explicit binding to Tk 8.0+ only (preventing 9.0+ to be accepted).

author: ojaywillow
body:
## Problem
The `/api/tasks` endpoint was taking **~10 seconds** to load due to:

1. **N+1 Query Problem**: For each task, a separate DB query was run to get `pending_applications_count`
   - 20 tasks = 20 extra queries

2. **Translation API Calls**: For each task, 2 HTTP calls to Google Translate (title + description)
   - 20 tasks = 40 API calls with 5 second timeout each
   - If API is slow, this compounds terribly

## Solution

### 1. Fixed N+1 Queries (`crud.py`)
**Before:**
```python
for task in tasks:
    task_dict['pending_applications_count'] = get_pending_applications_count(task.id)  # 1 query each!
```

**After:**
```python
# Single query for ALL tasks
pending_counts = get_pending_applications_counts(task_ids)  # 1 query total
for task_dict in tasks_list:
    task_dict['pending_applications_count'] = pending_counts.get(task_id, 0)
```

### 2. Optimized Translation Service (`translation.py`)
- **Fast path**: Skip immediately if no API key configured
- **Cached check**: Result of `is_translation_enabled()` is cached
- **Reduced timeout**: 5s → 2s (fail fast)
- **Better caching**: Check for existing cache entry before inserting

## Performance Impact

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| DB queries | 21+ | 2 |
| API calls (no key) | 40 | 0 |
| API calls (with key) | 40 | 40 (cached after first) |
| Response time (no translation) | ~10s | <100ms |
| Response time (with translation) | ~10s | <500ms (cached) |

## Testing
```bash
# Start backend
python wsgi.py

# Test endpoint
curl "http://localhost:5000/api/tasks?per_page=20"

# Should return in <1 second now
```

## Files Changed
- `app/routes/tasks/crud.py` - Batch queries for pending counts

author: bolt-dee
body:
## Pull Request Description

### Overview
This PR introduces the Axiom Action Approval smart contract, a Clarity-based on-chain governance system for AI agent actions on the Stacks blockchain. The contract implements a transparent approval workflow where owners review and approve or reject AI agent requests before execution, enabling human-in-the-loop oversight for critical operations.

### Changes
- **New Contract**: `axiom-action-approval.clar` - Complete governance smart contract implementation
- **Core Features**:
  - Action request system for AI agents to submit requests for owner review
  - Owner approval/rejection gate for pending actions
  - Execution control restricting agents to approved actions only
  - Immutable audit trail with burn-block-height timestamps
  - Role-based access control (owner/agent verification)
  - Real-time action metadata and counting functions

### Contract Functions Implemented

**Agent Functions:**
- `request-action(owner, description)` - Submit action request for owner approval with human-readable description
- `execute-action(id)` - Execute a previously approved action

**Owner Functions:**
- `approve-action(id)` - Approve a pending action request
- `reject-action(id)` - Reject and close a pending action request

**Read-Only Functions:**
- `get-action(id)` - Query complete action details (owner, agent, description, approval/execution status, timestamp)
- `action-count` - Get total number of actions created

### Technical Implementation

- **State Management**: 
  - `next-action-id` variable maintains auto-incrementing action counter
  - `actions` map stores action metadata with owner, agent, description, approval status, execution status, and creation timestamp

- **Action Lifecycle**: REQUEST (agent) → APPROVE/REJECT (owner) → EXECUTE (agent)

- **Access Control**: Principal-based verification ensures owners can only approve/reject their own actions and agents can only execute actions they requested

- **Immutable Audit Trail**: All actions timestamped with burn-block-height for complete governance history

- **Error Handling**: 5 distinct error codes (u100-u104) for comprehensive failure scenarios

### Testing Checklist

- [ ] Test AI agents can create action requests with descriptions
- [ ] Verify owners can approve pending actions
- [ ] Verify owners can reject pending actions
- [ ] Test approved actions can be executed by agents
- [ ] Verify ERR-NOT-OWNER prevents non-owners from approving/rejecting (u100)
- [ ] Verify ERR-NOT-AGENT prevents non-agents from executing (u101)
- [ ] Test ERR-NOT-FOUND for non-existent action IDs (u102)
- [ ] Verify ERR-NOT-APPROVED prevents execution of unapproved actions (u103)
- [ ] Test ERR-ALREADY-USED prevents re-execution or execution after rejection (u104)
- [ ] Verify action-count increments with each new request
- [ ] Test get-action returns accurate metadata for each action
- [ ] Verify rejected actions cannot be executed
- [ ] Test multiple concurrent actions with correct state tracking

### Security Considerations

- **Principal Verification**: All restricted functions verify caller identity to prevent unauthorized approvals/rejections
- **One-Time Execution**: Executed or rejected actions are immutable and cannot be reused
- **Owner-Only Approvals**: Only action owners can approve or reject their own actions
- **Agent-Only Execution**: Only designated agents can execute actions they created
- **Immutable Audit Trail**: All actions permanently recorded on-chain with timestamps for compliance

### Deployment Notes

- Contract deploys to Stacks network with auto-incrementing action ID counter starting at 0
- All principals verified for ownership and agency relationships
- Off-chain execution handlers responsible for actual business logic after on-chain approval
- No fund transfers or external dependencies

**Contract**: axiom-action-approval.clar  
**Network**: Stacks (STX)  
**Language**: Clarity  
**Purpose**: AI Agent Action Approval Gate & Governance

## Summary

Add conformance tests to verify localhost MCP servers properly validate Host headers to prevent DNS rebinding attacks.

Closes #103

## Changes

### New scenario: `dns-rebinding-protection`

Two checks:
- **`localhost-host-rebinding-rejected`**: Server returns 4xx for non-localhost Host headers (e.g., `Host: evil.example.com`)
- **`localhost-host-valid-accepted`**: Server accepts valid localhost Host headers

### Implementation details

- Uses `undici` for making HTTP requests with custom Host headers (native fetch doesn't allow this)
- Accepts any 4xx status code as valid rejection (403, 421, etc.)
- Tests require localhost server URL - non-localhost URLs return FAILURE with clear message

### Additional changes

- Updated `everything-server` example to use `createMcpExpressApp()` for DNS rebinding protection
- Added negative test case `no-dns-rebinding-protection.ts` that intentionally omits protection

## Testing

Verified against:
- ✅ TypeScript SDK (everything-server with `createMcpExpressApp()`)
- ✅ Python SDK (everything-server with auto-enabled protection)
- ✅ Negative test case (correctly fails)

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure the custom auth flow issues Supabase-compatible JWTs so Postgres RLS using `auth.role()` / `auth.jwt()` works. 
- Propagate the custom access token into the app's Supabase client so all DB requests send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and offline/PIN unlock behaviour still works. 
- Surface clear diagnostics and UI feedback for token / RLS failures instead of treating DB 403s as generic auth failures.

### Description
- Backend: changed the custom login endpoint to sign access tokens with `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` and include `sub`, `role: 'authenticated'`, `email`, `event_id`, `station_id`, `sessionId` and reasonable `exp` (`web/api/auth/login.ts`).
- Supabase client: added `createSupabaseClient` + `setSupabaseAccessToken` helper and expose a mutable `supabase` instance that is recreated with `global.headers.Authorization` when token changes and also sets realtime auth (`web/src/supabaseClient.ts`).
- Auth flow: validate and decode the JWT on login/bootstrap/unlock, log claims in dev, set the Supabase access token after successful login or PIN unlock, and clear it on logout (`web/src/auth/context.tsx`).
- App diagnostics / error handling: added `reportSupabaseError` to log request status/messages in dev and show a clear access-denied banner `"Účet není přiřazen k tomuto stanovišti…"` on 403s; outbox sync now uses the cached access token instead of relying on `supabase.auth` session (`web/src/App.tsx`).
- UX/messages: added shared messages and translated login error mappings for invalid/missing JWTs and access-denied cases (`web/src/auth/messages.ts`, `web/src/auth/loginErrors.ts`).
- Tests: unit test `vi.mock` updated to provide `setSupabaseAccessToken` so the test environment can accept the new helper (`web/src/__tests__/stationFlow.test.tsx`).

### Testing
- Unit tests: mocks updated (`stationFlow.test.tsx`) to include `setSupabaseAccessToken`; the full test suite was not executed in this change. 
- Manual/dev diagnostics: JWT claims are logged in `DEV` builds when tokens are loaded or validated, and 403s now set an explicit access-denied UI banner; these diagnostics were added to help validate behavior during runtime.
